bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第178卷卷第一百七十八

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 178, Volume One Hundred Seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 178.

sentences.zh: 【隋紀二】 起玄黓困敦，盡屠維協洽，凡八年。

translations.literal: [Sui Annals 2] Beginning with Xuanyi Kundun, ending with Tuwei Xiehe; eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Sui Annals 2] From the year Xuanyi Kundun through Tuwei Xiehe—eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，己巳，以蜀王秀為內史令兼右領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on jisi, the Prince of Shu, Xiu, was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Right Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on jisi, Prince Xiu of Shu was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Right Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 國子博士何妥與尚書右僕射邳公蘇威爭議事，積不相能。

translations.literal: The National University academician He Tuo and the Minister of the Right, Duke of Pi Su Wei, disputed affairs and over time could not get along.
translations.idiomatic: National University academician He Tuo and the Minister of the Right, Duke of Pi Su Wei, clashed over policy and grew increasingly hostile to each other.

sentences.zh: 威子夔為太子通事舍人，少敏辯，有盛名，士大夫多附之。

translations.literal: Wei's son Kui served as Attendant Censor of the Crown Prince; young, clever in debate, with great renown; many literati attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's son Kui served as an attendant censor to the crown prince. Still young, he was quick-witted and eloquent and enjoyed wide fame, and many gentlemen of the court rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 及議樂，夔與妥各有所持；

translations.literal: When music was discussed, Kui and Tuo each held to his own view;
translations.idiomatic: When court debated ritual music, Kui and Tuo each stood by his own position;

sentences.zh: 詔百僚署其所同，百僚以威故，同夔者什八九。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the hundred officials to sign which side they agreed with; because of Wei, eight or nine tenths agreed with Kui.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered the hundred officials to sign which view they endorsed. Out of deference to Wei, eight or nine tenths sided with Kui.

sentences.zh: 妥恚曰：「吾席間函丈四十餘年，反為昨暮兒之所屈邪！」

translations.literal: Tuo angrily said: "I have lectured at my desk for more than forty years—am I to be brought low by a boy of yesterday evening!"
translations.idiomatic: Tuo fumed: "I have taught from my lectern for more than forty years—am I really to be bested by some stripling who only rose yesterday?"

sentences.zh: 遂奏：「威與禮部尚書盧愷、吏部侍郎薛道衡、尚書右丞王弘、考功侍郎李同和等共為朋黨。

translations.literal: He then memorialized: "Wei together with the Minister of Rites Lu Kai, Vice Minister of Personnel Xue Daoheng, Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Hong, Vice Director of Examinations Li Tonghe, and others have formed a faction.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial: "Wei has formed a clique with Minister of Rites Lu Kai, Vice Minister of Personnel Xue Daoheng, Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Hong, Vice Director of Examinations Li Tonghe, and others.

sentences.zh: 省中呼弘為世子，同和為叔，言二人如威之子弟也。」

translations.literal: Within the ministry they called Hong 'the heir' and Tonghe 'the uncle,' saying the two were like Wei's sons."
translations.idiomatic: Inside the ministry they nicknamed Hong 'the heir' and Tonghe 'the uncle,' as though the two were Wei's own sons."

sentences.zh: 復言威以曲道任其從父弟徹、肅罔冒為官等數事。

translations.literal: He further said that Wei by improper means had his cousins Che and Su appointed to office through false claims on several counts.
translations.idiomatic: He further charged that Wei had used back channels to secure official posts for his cousins Che and Su through fraudulent claims on several counts.

sentences.zh: 上命蜀王秀、上柱國虞慶則等雜案之，事頗有狀。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Prince of Shu Xiu, Grand General Yu Qingze, and others jointly to investigate; the matters largely matched the charges.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Prince Xiu of Shu, Grand General Yu Qingze, and others to investigate jointly. On most points the accusations held up.

sentences.zh: 上大怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙巳，威坐免官爵，以開府儀同三司就第；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on yisi, Wei was stripped of office and rank and given the concurrent title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equipage, and returned to his residence;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on yisi, Wei was removed from office and stripped of his titles, granted the nominal rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equipage, and sent home;

sentences.zh: 盧愷除名，知名之士坐威得罪者百餘人。

translations.literal: Lu Kai was struck from the rolls; more than a hundred men of note implicated through Wei were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai was struck from the rolls, and more than a hundred prominent men who fell with Wei were punished.

sentences.zh: 初，周室以來，選無清濁；

translations.literal: Initially, since the Zhou house, selection had no distinction of pure and impure;
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhou dynasty onward, official selection had drawn no clear line between worthy and unworthy candidates;

sentences.zh: 及愷攝吏部，與薛道衡等甄別士流，故涉朋黨之謗，以至得罪。

translations.literal: when Kai took charge of the Ministry of Personnel and together with Xue Daoheng and others sifted the gentry, he therefore became embroiled in factional slander and reached punishment.
translations.idiomatic: when Kai took charge of the Ministry of Personnel and, with Xue Daoheng and others, sorted the gentry into ranks, he drew factional accusations and was punished in the end.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上曰：「蘇威德行者，但為人所誤耳！」

translations.literal: Before long the emperor said: "Su Wei is a man of virtue—he was only led astray by others!"
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor said, "Su Wei is a man of real moral weight—he was simply misled by others!"

sentences.zh: 命之通籍。

translations.literal: He ordered him restored to court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him restored to attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 威好立條章，每歲責民間五品不遜，或答云：「管內無五品之家。」

translations.literal: Wei liked to establish regulations; each year he required reports of the five grades of unfilial conduct among the people, and some answered: "Within our district there are no households of the fifth grade."
translations.idiomatic: Wei loved to lay down rules. Each year he demanded reports of the five grades of unfilial conduct in the populace, and some districts replied, "There are no fifth-grade households within our jurisdiction."

sentences.zh: 其不相應領，類多如此。

translations.literal: Such mismatches between regulation and reality were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Mismatches between his regulations and local reality were common.

sentences.zh: 又為餘糧簿，欲使有無相贍；

translations.literal: He also made a surplus-grain register, intending that those with surplus and those without should support one another;
translations.idiomatic: He also devised a surplus-grain register, hoping to let households with grain and those without share among themselves;

sentences.zh: 民部侍郎郎茂以為煩迂不急，皆奏罷之。

translations.literal: the Vice Minister of Revenue Lang Mao deemed these vexatious, roundabout, and not urgent, and memorialized to abolish them all.
translations.idiomatic: but Vice Minister of Revenue Lang Mao judged them cumbersome, impractical, and not urgent, and memorialized to abolish them all.

sentences.zh: 茂，基之子也，嘗為衛國令。

translations.literal: Mao was Ji's son; he had once been magistrate of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was the son of Ji and had once served as magistrate of Wei.

sentences.zh: 有民張元預兄弟不睦，丞、尉請加嚴刑，茂曰：「元預兄弟本相憎疾，又坐得罪，彌益其仇，非化民之意也。」

translations.literal: A commoner Zhang Yuanyu and his brothers were not harmonious; the assistant magistrate and sheriff requested severe punishment. Mao said: "Yuanyu and his brothers originally hated one another; to punish them as well would only deepen their enmity—this is not the intent of transforming the people."
translations.idiomatic: When a commoner named Zhang Yuanyu and his brothers fell out, the assistant magistrate and sheriff asked for harsh punishment. Mao said, "The Yuanyu brothers already despise each other. To punish them now would only deepen their hatred. That is not how one transforms the people."

sentences.zh: 乃徐諭之以義。

translations.literal: He then slowly instructed them in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He then gently taught them what was right.

sentences.zh: 元預等各感悔，頓首請罪，遂相親睦，稱為友悌。

translations.literal: Yuanyu and the others were each moved to repentance, kowtowed to beg forgiveness, and thereafter were affectionate and harmonious, praised as fraternal.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu and his brothers were moved to repentance, kowtowed to beg forgiveness, and thereafter lived in harmony, praised as a model of brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 己巳，上享太廟。

translations.literal: On jisi the emperor offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the emperor offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 壬申晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On renshen, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 帝以天下用律者多春駁，罪同論異，八月，甲戌，制：諸州死罪，不得輒決，悉移大理按覆，事盡，然後上省奏裁。」

translations.literal: The emperor, because throughout the realm legal applications were many and erroneous, with the same crime receiving different verdicts, in the eighth month on jiaxu issued a regulation: death sentences in the various prefectures may not be decided summarily; all shall be transferred to the Court of Judicial Review for reinvestigation; when matters are complete, then report upward to the province for decision."
translations.idiomatic: Because legal judgments across the empire were often inconsistent—identical crimes receiving different sentences—the emperor in the eighth month, on jiaxu, decreed that no prefecture might execute a death sentence on its own. Every capital case was to be sent to the Court of Judicial Review for reinvestigation, and only after that process was finished might the province report upward for final approval."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬午，上享太廟。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renwu, the emperor offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renwu, the emperor offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛亥，祀南郊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, he sacrificed at the southern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, he sacrificed at the southern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 己未，新義公韓擒虎卒。

translations.literal: On jiwei the Duke of Xinyi Han Qianhu died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei the Duke of Xinyi, Han Qianhu, died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙酉，以內史令楊素為尚書右僕射，與高熲專掌朝政。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, the Director of the Palace Secretariat Yang Su was made Minister of the Right and together with Gao Jiong exclusively wielded court governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, Yang Su was moved from Director of the Palace Secretariat to Minister of the Right and, with Gao Jiong, took sole charge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 素性疏辯，高下在心，朝臣之內，頗推高熲，敬牛弘，厚接薛道衡，視蘇威蔑如也，自餘朝貴，多被陵轢。

translations.literal: Su was by nature unrestrained in speech, high and low in his own heart; among court ministers he fairly esteemed Gao Jiong, respected Niu Hong, treated Xue Daoheng warmly, looked down on Su Wei as nothing, and the rest of the court nobility he often bullied.
translations.idiomatic: Su was loose-tongued and self-willed. Among his colleagues he fairly esteemed Gao Jiong, respected Niu Hong, and treated Xue Daoheng warmly, but looked on Su Wei with contempt and bullied most other court grandees.

sentences.zh: 其才藝風調優於熲；

translations.literal: His talent, artistry, and bearing were superior to Jiong's;
translations.idiomatic: In talent, polish, and personal style he outshone Jiong;

sentences.zh: 至於推誠體國，處物平當，有宰相識度，不如熲遠矣。

translations.literal: but in sincerity toward the state, fair handling of affairs, and the measure of a chancellor, he was far inferior to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: yet in sincerity toward the state, evenhanded judgment, and true chancellorial breadth he fell far short of Jiong.

sentences.zh: 右領軍大將軍賀若弼，自謂功名出朝臣之右，每以宰相自許。

translations.literal: The Right Commander-in-Chief He Ruo Bi, considering his merit and fame above the court ministers, often regarded himself as fit for the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Commander-in-Chief He Ruo Bi believed his achievements outranked every minister at court and constantly treated himself as a chancellor in waiting.

sentences.zh: 既而楊素為僕射，弼仍為將軍，甚不平，形於言色，由是坐免官，怨望愈甚。

translations.literal: Then Yang Su became Vice Director but Bi remained a general; he was very discontent, which showed in his words and face; hence he was dismissed from office, and his resentment grew.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Su became Vice Director while Bi remained only a general, Bi grew bitter, and his resentment showed plainly in word and face. He was stripped of office, and his discontent only deepened.

sentences.zh: 久之，上下弼獄，謂之曰：「我以高熲、楊素為宰相，汝每昌言曰：『此二人惟堪啖飯耳！』

translations.literal: After a long time the emperor summoned Bi to prison and said to him: "I take Gao Jiong and Yang Su as chancellors; you often loudly say: 'These two are fit only for eating rice!
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the emperor had Bi brought before him in custody and said, "I have made Gao Jiong and Yang Su my chancellors, yet you keep proclaiming aloud, 'Those two are fit for nothing but eating rice!

sentences.zh: 是何意也？」

translations.literal: What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you mean by that?"

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「熲，臣之敵人；

translations.literal: Bi said: "Jiong is my enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "Jiong is my enemy;

sentences.zh: 素，臣舅子。

translations.literal: Su is my wife's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Su is my wife's nephew.

sentences.zh: 臣並知其為人，誠有此語。」

translations.literal: Your servant knows both their characters—I truly said this."
translations.idiomatic: I know both men well, and I did say exactly that."

sentences.zh: 公卿奏弼怨望，罪當死。

translations.literal: The high officials memorialized that Bi was resentful and should die.
translations.idiomatic: The high officials memorialized that Bi was seditious in spirit and deserved death.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「臣下守法不移，公可自求活理。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "A minister who keeps the law without wavering—the duke may seek for himself a reason to live."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A subject who holds to the law without wavering may yet plead for his own life. Duke, find your own grounds to live."

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「臣恃至尊威靈，將八千兵渡江，擒陳叔寶，竊以此望活。」

translations.literal: Bi said: "Your servant relied on Your Majesty's awesome majesty, led eight thousand troops across the river, and captured Chen Shubao—I venture to hope to live by this merit."
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Your servant, relying on Your Majesty's awesome majesty, led eight thousand men across the Yangzi and captured Chen Shubao. I venture to hope that merit may spare my life."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此已格外重賞，何用追論！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That already received an exceptional grand reward—why bring it up again!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You were already rewarded far beyond the norm for that. Why bring it up again?"

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「臣已蒙格外重賞，今還格外望活。」

translations.literal: Bi said: "Your servant has already received an exceptional grand reward; now I again hope exceptionally to live."
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "I have already received an exceptional reward; now I ask for an exceptional reprieve."

sentences.zh: 既而上低回者數日，惜其功，特令除名。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor hesitated for several days, cherished his merit, and specially ordered only removal from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brooded for several days, reluctant to lose so great a warrior, and specially ordered only that Bi be struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復其爵位，上亦忌之，不復任使，然每宴賜，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: After more than a year his title was restored; the emperor also was wary of him and did not again employ him, yet at every feast and gift he treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year his titles were restored, but the emperor still distrusted him and gave him no office. Even so, whenever Bi appeared at court banquets the emperor treated him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 有司上言：「府藏皆滿，無所容，積於廊廡。」

translations.literal: The responsible office reported: "The treasuries are all full with no room; goods are piled in the corridors."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported, "The treasuries are full to bursting with nowhere left to store goods, which are now piled in the corridors."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕既薄賦於民，又大經賜用，何得爾也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have already lightly taxed the people and greatly increased gifts and expenditure—how can it be thus?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have kept taxes light and lavished gifts on a grand scale—how can the treasuries still overflow?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「入者常多於出，略計每年賜用，至數百萬段，曾無減省。」

translations.literal: They replied: "Income has regularly exceeded outgo; roughly calculated, each year's gifts and expenditure reach millions of bolts, never diminishing."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Receipts still regularly exceed disbursements. Even your annual gifts and grants run to millions of bolts of cloth, and that figure has never fallen."

sentences.zh: 於是更辟左藏院以受之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they newly opened the left treasury courtyard to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore opened a new left treasury courtyard to hold the surplus.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「寧積於人，無藏府庫。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Better to accumulate among the people than to hoard in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "Better that wealth rest with the people than pile up in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 河北、河東今年田租三分減一，兵減半功，調全免。」

translations.literal: In Hebei and Hedong this year's land tax is reduced by one-third; corvée labor is halved; levies are entirely exempted."
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei and Hedong this year's land tax shall be cut by one-third, corvée labor halved, and all levies waived entirely."

sentences.zh: 時天下戶口歲增，京輔及三河地少而人眾，衣食不給，帝乃發使四出，均天下之田，其狹鄉每丁才至二十畝，老少又少焉。

translations.literal: At this time household registers increased yearly; the capital region and the three rivers had little land and many people; food and clothing were insufficient; the emperor then sent envoys in four directions to equalize land throughout the realm; in narrow districts each adult male got only twenty mu; old and young received even less.
translations.idiomatic: Household registers were growing year by year, yet around the capital and along the three rivers there was too little land for too many people, and food and clothing ran short. The emperor therefore sent envoys in all directions to equalize landholding across the empire. In cramped districts each adult male received as little as twenty mu, and the old and young even less.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬子，上祀感生帝。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renzi, the emperor sacrificed to the Lord of Life-procreating.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renzi, the emperor sacrificed to the Lord of Life-procreating.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，行幸岐州。

translations.literal: On renxu he traveled in favor to Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the emperor traveled to Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙午，詔營仁壽宮於岐州之北，使楊素監之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingwu, an edict ordered the building of Renshou Palace north of Qi Prefecture, with Yang Su to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingwu, he decreed the construction of Renshou Palace north of Qi Prefecture and put Yang Su in charge.

sentences.zh: 素奏前萊州刺史宇文愷檢校將作大匠，記室封德彝為土木監。

translations.literal: Su memorialized the former governor of Laizhou Yu Wenkai as chief inspector of palace construction and the recorder Feng Deyi as supervisor of earthworks.
translations.idiomatic: Su recommended the former governor of Laizhou, Yu Wenkai, as chief inspector of palace construction and his recorder Feng Deyi as supervisor of earthworks.

sentences.zh: 於是夷山堙谷以立宮殿，崇台累榭，宛轉相屬。

translations.literal: Thereupon they leveled mountains and filled valleys to erect palaces; lofty terraces and piled pavilions wound and connected with one another.
translations.idiomatic: Workers leveled mountains and filled valleys to raise palaces, lofty terraces, and tiered pavilions that wound together in endless succession.

sentences.zh: 役使嚴急，丁夫多死，疲屯顛仆，推填坑坎，覆以土石，因而築為平地。

translations.literal: Labor service was harsh and urgent; many corvée workers died; exhausted they collapsed; they were pushed into pit ditches, covered with earth and stone, and thus built as level ground.
translations.idiomatic: Labor was driven with brutal urgency. Countless corvée workers died; when the exhausted collapsed, they were shoved into pits, covered with earth and stone, and the ground was built up over them.

sentences.zh: 死者以萬數。

translations.literal: The dead numbered in the ten thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The dead ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，上至自岐州。

translations.literal: On dinghai the emperor returned from Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the emperor returned from Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己卯，立皇孫暕為豫章王。

translations.literal: On jimao he established the imperial grandson Zhan as Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao he enfeoffed his grandson Zhan as Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 暕，廣之子也。

translations.literal: Zhan was Guang's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was the son of Yang Guang.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，制：「私家不得藏緯候、圖讖。」

translations.literal: On dingyou a regulation: "Private persons may not hoard weft charts and prophecy charts."
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the emperor decreed, "Private households may not keep astrological weft texts or prophecy charts."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊辰晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuchen, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuchen, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 是歲，上命禮部尚書牛弘等議明堂制度。

translations.literal: This year the emperor ordered the Minister of Rites Niu Hong and others to discuss regulations for the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor ordered Minister of Rites Niu Hong and others to debate the regulations for the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 宇文愷獻明堂木樣，上命有司規度安業裡地，將立之；

translations.literal: Yu Wenkai presented a wooden model of the Bright Hall; the emperor ordered the officials to survey and fix land in Anye Ward to erect it;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenkai presented a wooden model of the Bright Hall, and the emperor ordered officials to survey a site in Anye Ward for its construction;

sentences.zh: 而諸儒異議，久之不決，乃罷之。

translations.literal: but the various Ru scholars differed; after a long time no decision was reached, and the project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: but the Confucian scholars quarreled for so long that no decision could be reached, and the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 上之滅陳也，以陳叔寶屏風賜突厥大義公主。

translations.literal: When the emperor destroyed Chen, he gave Chen Shubao's screen to the Tujue Princess of Great Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Chen, the emperor gave Chen Shubao's painted screen to the Türk Princess of Great Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 公主以其宗國之覆，心常不平，書屏風，為詩敘陳亡以自寄。

translations.literal: The princess, because her ancestral state had been overthrown, was always ill at ease in heart; she wrote on the screen poems narrating Chen's fall to express her feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Because her native state had been destroyed, the princess brooded constantly. She wrote on the screen poems recounting Chen's fall to give voice to her grief.

sentences.zh: 上聞而惡之，禮賜漸薄。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he disliked it; ritual gifts gradually grew thin.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this he took offense, and the gifts sent to her grew steadily meager.

sentences.zh: 彭公劉昶先尚周公主，流人楊欽亡入突厥，詐言昶欲與其妻作亂攻隋，遣欽來密告大義公主，發兵擾邊。

translations.literal: The Duke of Peng Liu Chang had earlier married a Zhou princess; the exile Yang Qin fled into the Türks and falsely claimed that Chang wished with his wife to rebel and attack Sui, sending Qin to secretly inform the Princess of Great Righteousness to raise troops and harass the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Peng, Liu Chang, had earlier married a princess of Zhou. The exile Yang Qin fled to the Türks and falsely claimed that Chang and his wife were plotting rebellion against Sui. He sent Qin to inform the Princess of Great Righteousness in secret and urge her to raise troops and harass the frontier.

sentences.zh: 都藍可汗信之，乃不修職貢，頗為邊患。

translations.literal: Khan Dulou believed it; he ceased presenting tribute and became quite a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: Khan Dulou believed him, stopped sending tribute, and became a serious border threat.

sentences.zh: 上遣車騎將軍長孫晟使於突厥，微觀察之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the General of the Palace Cavalry Zhangsun Sheng as envoy to the Türks to observe subtly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent General of the Palace Cavalry Zhangsun Sheng to the Türks to observe matters discreetly.

sentences.zh: 公主見晟，言辭不遜，又遣所私胡人安遂迦與楊欽計議，扇惑都藍。

translations.literal: The princess saw Sheng; her words were impertinent; she also sent her private Hu retainer An Suijia with Yang Qin to plot and incite Dulou.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess met Sheng her words were insolent. She also sent her private Hu retainer An Suijia to plot with Yang Qin and stir up Dulou against Sui.

sentences.zh: 晟至京師，具以狀聞。

translations.literal: Sheng reached the capital and reported the full situation.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng returned to the capital and reported everything in full.

sentences.zh: 上遣晟往索欽；

translations.literal: The emperor sent Sheng to demand Qin;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Sheng back to demand Yang Qin's extradition;

sentences.zh: 都藍不與，曰：「檢校客內無此色人。」

translations.literal: Dulou would not give him up, saying: "Among the guests under inspection there is no person of this description."
translations.idiomatic: Dulou refused, saying, "Among the guests in my camp there is no man of that description."

sentences.zh: 晟乃賂其達官，知欽所在。

translations.literal: Sheng then bribed his high officials and learned where Qin was.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng then bribed Dulou's senior officials and learned where Qin was hiding.

sentences.zh: 夜，掩獲之，以示都藍，因發公主私事，國人大以為恥。

translations.literal: By night he seized him by surprise, showed him to Dulou, and thereby exposed the princess's private affairs; the countrymen were greatly shamed.
translations.idiomatic: By night he seized Qin by surprise and presented him to Dulou, exposing the princess's secret affairs in the process. The Türk nobles were deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 都藍執安遂迦等，並以付晟。

translations.literal: Dulou seized An Suijia and the others and handed them all to Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dulou arrested An Suijia and the others and handed them all over to Sheng.

sentences.zh: 上大喜，加授開府儀同三司，仍遣入突厥廢公主。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, additionally appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equipage, and still sent him into the Türks to depose the princess.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, promoted Sheng to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equipage, and sent him back into the Türk lands to depose the princess.

sentences.zh: 內史侍郎裴矩請說都藍使殺公主。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Vice Director Pei Ju requested persuading Dulou to kill the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Vice Director Pei Ju proposed persuading Dulou to kill the princess.

sentences.zh: 時處羅侯之子染干，號突利可汗，居北方，遣使求婚，上使裴矩謂之曰：「當殺大義公主，乃許婚。」

translations.literal: At that time Chuluohou's son Ran'gan, titled Khan Tuli, dwelt in the north; he sent an envoy to request marriage. The emperor had Pei Ju tell him: "When the Princess of Great Righteousness is killed, then marriage will be granted."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chuluohou's son Ran'gan, known as Khan Tuli, lived in the north and sent envoys to request a marriage alliance. The emperor had Pei Ju tell him, "Kill the Princess of Great Righteousness, and the marriage will be granted."

sentences.zh: 突利復譖之於都藍，都藍因發怒，殺公主，更表請婚，朝議將許之。

translations.literal: Tuli again slandered this to Dulou; Dulou therefore grew angry, killed the princess, again memorialized requesting marriage, and court discussion was about to consent.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli slandered Dulou again in the matter. Dulou flew into a rage, killed the princess, and memorialized anew to request marriage. Court opinion was leaning toward consent.

sentences.zh: 長孫晟曰：「臣觀雍虞閭反覆無信，直以與玷厥有隙，所以欲依倚國家，雖與為婚，終當叛去。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Sheng said: "Your servant observes that Yongyu Lubu is treacherous and untrustworthy; merely because he has a rift with Bianjue he wishes to rely on the state. Even if given marriage, he will ultimately desert.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Sheng said, "Your servant finds Yongyu Lubu treacherous and faithless. He seeks our support only because he is at odds with Bianjue. Even if we marry him a princess, he will rebel in the end.

sentences.zh: 今若得尚公主，承藉威靈，玷厥、染干必受其征發。

translations.literal: If he now obtains an imperial princess in marriage, drawing on imperial majesty, Bianjue and Ran'gan will surely be subjected to his conscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: If he gains an imperial princess now, he will borrow our prestige to conscript Bianjue and Ran'gan.

sentences.zh: 強而更反，後恐難圖。

translations.literal: When strong he will rebel again; afterward he will be hard to scheme against.
translations.idiomatic: Once he grows strong he will turn against us again, and then he will be far harder to control.

sentences.zh: 且染干者，處羅侯之子，素有誠款，於今兩代，前乞通婚，不如許之，招令南徙，兵少力弱，易可撫馴，使敵雍虞閭以為邊捍。」

translations.literal: Moreover Ran'gan is Chuluohou's son, always sincere through two generations; earlier he begged for marriage—better to consent, summon him south to settle; his troops are few and strength weak, easy to soothe and tame, and make him enemy to Yongyu Lubu as a border defense."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Ran'gan is Chuluohou's son and has shown good faith across two reigns. He has long sought marriage with us. Better to grant it, summon him south to settle, and use his small, weak force as a tame buffer against Yongyu Lubu."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 復遣晟慰諭染干，許尚公主。

translations.literal: He again sent Sheng to comfort and instruct Ran'gan and promised him marriage to an imperial princess.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Sheng to reassure Ran'gan and promised him an imperial princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 牛弘使協律郎范陽祖孝孫等參定雅樂，從陳陽山太守毛爽受京房律法，布管飛灰，順月皆驗。

translations.literal: Niu Hong had the Collaborative Rhythm Officer Zu Xiaosun of Fanyang and others fix orthodox music; from Chen's Yangshan prefect Mao Shuang they received Jing Fang's pitch law; laid pipes with flying ash; aligned with the months—all verified.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong had the Collaborative Rhythm Officer Zu Xiaosun of Fanyang and others set the court's orthodox music. From Chen's former Yangshan prefect Mao Shuang they received Jing Fang's pitch pipes and flying-ash method; month by month the tuning proved correct.

sentences.zh: 又每律生五音，十二律為六十音，因而六之，為三百六十音，分直一歲之日以配七音，而旋相為宮之法，由是著名。

translations.literal: Also each pitch produced five tones; twelve pitches made sixty tones; further multiplying by six made three hundred sixty tones, dividing to match the days of a year to pair with seven tones; the method of rotating to form the palace thereby became famous.
translations.idiomatic: Each pitch generated five tones; twelve pitches yielded sixty tones, and multiplying by six produced three hundred sixty tones, apportioned across the days of the year and matched to the seven scale degrees. The method of cyclically shifting the tonal center thereby won renown.

sentences.zh: 弘等乃奏下請復用旋宮法，上猶記何妥之言，注弘奏下，不聽作旋宮，但用黃鐘一宮。

translations.literal: Hong and the others then memorialized requesting restoration of the rotating-palace method; the emperor still remembered He Tuo's words, annotated Hong's memorial below, would not permit the rotating palace, and used only the single palace of Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and his colleagues then memorialized to revive the rotating-palace method, but the emperor still recalled He Tuo's objections. He annotated the memorial and refused the rotating palace, allowing only the single Yellow Bell mode.

sentences.zh: 於是弘等復為奏，附順上意，其前代金石並銷毀之，以息異議。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hong and the others again memorialized, conforming to the emperor's intent; the metal and stone instruments of former ages were all destroyed to quell dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and his colleagues memorialized again in line with the emperor's wishes. The metal and stone instruments of earlier dynasties were destroyed to silence further debate.

sentences.zh: 弘等又作武舞，以象隋之功德；

translations.literal: Hong and the others also composed a martial dance to symbolize Sui's merit and virtue;
translations.idiomatic: They also composed a martial dance to embody Sui's achievements;

sentences.zh: 郊廟饗用一調，迎氣用五調。

translations.literal: suburban and temple feasts used one mode; welcoming the qi used five modes.
translations.idiomatic: suburban and temple sacrifices used one mode, while the rites for welcoming the seasonal qi used five.

sentences.zh: 舊工稍盡，其餘聲律，皆不復通。

translations.literal: Old craftsmen gradually died out; the rest of the pitch laws were no longer understood.
translations.idiomatic: The old masters gradually passed away, and the finer points of pitch and rhythm were lost.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，樂成。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, the music was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, the new music was finished.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙丑，詔行新樂，且曰：「民間音樂，流僻日久，棄其舊體，競造繁聲，宜加禁約，務存其本。」

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yichou, an edict ordered the new music performed, and said: "Popular music has long been dissolute and eccentric, abandoning its old forms and competing to create ornate sounds—restrictions should be strengthened to preserve the root."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yichou, an edict ordered the new music performed and declared, "Popular music has grown decadent for years, abandoning its proper forms in favor of ornate sounds. It should be restricted so that the tradition may be preserved."

sentences.zh: 萬寶常聽太常所奏樂，泫然泣曰：「樂聲淫厲而哀，天下不久將盡！」

translations.literal: Wan Baochang heard the music performed by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, wept and said: "The music is licentious, harsh, and mournful—the realm will soon perish!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wan Baochang heard the Court of Imperial Sacrifices perform the new music, he wept and said, "This music is licentious, harsh, and mournful. The realm will not last much longer!"

sentences.zh: 時四海全盛，聞者皆謂不然；

translations.literal: At that time the four seas were in full prosperity; those who heard all said it was not so;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the empire was at its height, and everyone who heard him dismissed the prophecy;

sentences.zh: 大業之末，其言卒驗。

translations.literal: at the end of the Daye reign his words were finally verified.
translations.idiomatic: yet by the end of the Daye reign his words had come true.

sentences.zh: 寶常貧而無子，久之，竟餓死。

translations.literal: Baochang was poor and childless; after a long time he finally starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang lived in poverty and had no children. In time he starved to death.

sentences.zh: 且死，悉取其書燒之，曰：「用此何為！」

translations.literal: As he was dying he took all his books and burned them, saying: "What use is this!"
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he burned all his books, saying, "What good are these now?"

sentences.zh: 先是，台、省、府、寺及諸州皆置公廨錢，收息取給。

translations.literal: Earlier, the bureaus, ministries, offices, directorates, and all prefectures had established public-office funds, taking interest for supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Previously every ministry, office, directorate, and prefecture had maintained public-office funds that lived off interest income.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書蘇孝慈以為「官司出舉興生，煩擾百姓，敗損風俗，請皆禁止，給地以營農。」

translations.literal: The Minister of Works Su Xiaoci held that "when government offices lend money to generate profit, they vex the people and damage custom—request that all be forbidden and land given for farming."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Su Xiaoci argued that "when government offices lend money for profit they harass the people and corrupt public morals. All such lending should be banned, and land granted for farming instead."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁卯，始詔「公卿以下皆給職田，毋得治生，與民爭利。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingmao, he first decreed: "From the high ministers down, all shall be given official fields; they may not engage in trade or compete with the people for profit."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingmao, he decreed for the first time, "From the highest ministers down, all shall receive official fields. They may not engage in trade or compete with the people for profit."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙未，以邳公蘇威為納言。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on yiwei, Duke of Pi Su Wei was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on yiwei, Duke of Pi Su Wei was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，張賓歷既行，廣平劉孝孫及冀州秀才劉焯並言其失。

translations.literal: Initially, after Zhang Bin's calendar was put in use, Liu Xiaosun of Guangping and the Xiucai Liu Zhuo of Jizhou both spoke of its errors.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Bin's calendar had been adopted, Liu Xiaosun of Guangping and the Xiucai Liu Zhuo of Jizhou both pointed out its flaws.

sentences.zh: 賓方有寵於上，劉暉附會之，共短孝孫等，斥罷之。

translations.literal: Bin was then in favor with the emperor; Liu Hui attached himself to him; together they slandered Xiaosun and the others and had them dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was then in imperial favor, and Liu Hui sided with him. Together they slandered Xiaosun and the others until they were driven from office.

sentences.zh: 後賓卒，孝孫為掖縣丞，委官入京，上其事，詔留直太史，累年不調，乃抱其書，使弟子輿櫬來詣闕下，伏而慟哭；

translations.literal: Later Bin died; Xiaosun was assistant magistrate of Ye County; he resigned his office and entered the capital, submitted his work; an edict kept him at the Imperial Astronomer's office; for many years he received no promotion; then he embraced his books, had his disciples carry them in a coffin to the palace gate, and prostrated himself weeping;
translations.idiomatic: After Bin died, Xiaosun served as assistant magistrate of Ye. He resigned, went to the capital, and submitted his calendar. The court kept him at the Imperial Astronomer's office, but for years he received no promotion. At last he had his disciples carry his books in a coffin to the palace gate, where he prostrated himself and wept;

sentences.zh: 執法拘而奏之。

translations.literal: the law officers seized and reported him.
translations.idiomatic: the law officers seized him and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝異焉，以問國子祭酒何妥，妥言其善。

translations.literal: The emperor was struck by this and asked the National University Chancellor He Tuo; Tuo said it was good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was intrigued and asked National University Chancellor He Tuo, who praised Xiaosun's work.

sentences.zh: 乃遣與賓歷比較短長。

translations.literal: He then sent it to be compared in strengths and weaknesses with Bin's calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered it compared with Bin's calendar.

sentences.zh: 直太史勃海張冑玄與孝孫共短賓歷，異論鋒起，久之不定。

translations.literal: The Imperial Astronomer Zhang Zhouxuan of Bohai and Xiaosun together criticized Bin's calendar; conflicting opinions flared; for a long time no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Astronomer Zhang Zhouxuan of Bohai joined Xiaosun in attacking Bin's calendar. Debate raged for a long time without resolution.

sentences.zh: 上令參問日食事，楊素等奏：「太史凡奏日食二十有五，率皆無驗，冑玄所刻，前後妙中，孝孫所刻，驗亦過半。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered inquiry into solar eclipses; Yang Su and others memorialized: "The Imperial Astronomer in all reported twenty-five solar eclipses, almost none verified; Zhouxuan's calculations, before and after, were marvelously accurate; Xiaosun's calculations were verified in more than half."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a test based on solar eclipses. Yang Su and others reported, "The Imperial Astronomer's office has predicted twenty-five eclipses, almost none of which came true. Zhouxuan's calculations have been consistently accurate, and more than half of Xiaosun's have been verified as well."

sentences.zh: 於是上引孝孫、冑玄等親自勞徠。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor summoned Xiaosun, Zhouxuan, and the others and personally comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned Xiaosun, Zhouxuan, and the others and personally received them with honors.

sentences.zh: 孝孫請先斬劉暉，乃可定歷，帝不懌，又罷之。

translations.literal: Xiaosun requested that Liu Hui be beheaded first before the calendar could be fixed; the emperor was displeased and dismissed him again.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosun demanded that Liu Hui be executed before a new calendar could be adopted. The emperor took offense and dismissed him once more.

sentences.zh: 孝孫尋卒。

translations.literal: Xiaosun soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosun died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 關中大旱，民饑，上遣左右視民食，得豆屑雜糠以獻。

translations.literal: In Guanzhong a great drought; the people were hungry; the emperor sent attendants to observe the people's food and received bean husks mixed with chaff presented to him.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought struck Guanzhong and the people went hungry. The emperor sent attendants to inspect what the people were eating, and they brought back bean husks mixed with chaff.

sentences.zh: 上流涕以示群臣，深自咎責，為之不御酒肉者，殆將一期。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and showed it to the ministers, deeply blamed himself, and for nearly a full cycle abstained from wine and meat on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as he showed it to his ministers, blamed himself deeply, and for nearly a year abstained from wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛未，上帥民就食於洛陽，敕斥候不得輒有驅逼。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinwei, the emperor led the people to seek food in Luoyang and decreed that scouts might not casually drive or coerce them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinwei, the emperor led the people to Luoyang in search of food and decreed that scouts along the route might not harass or drive them on.

sentences.zh: 男女參廁於仗衛之間，遇扶老攜幼者，輒引馬避之，慰勉而去。

translations.literal: Men and women mingled among the armed guards; when he met those supporting the old and leading the young, he would rein in his horse to avoid them, comfort and encourage them, and pass on.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women mingled among his armed escort. Whenever he met people supporting the elderly or carrying children, he reined in his horse to give way, offered words of comfort, and moved on.

sentences.zh: 至艱險之處，見負擔者，令左右扶助之。

translations.literal: At difficult places, when he saw burden-bearers, he ordered his attendants to help them.
translations.idiomatic: At difficult stretches of road he ordered his attendants to help those carrying heavy loads.

sentences.zh: 冬，閏十月，甲寅，詔以齊、梁、陳宗祀廢絕，命高仁英、蕭琮、陳叔寶以時修祭，所須器物，有司給之。

translations.literal: In winter, the intercalary tenth month, on jiayin, an edict said that the ancestral sacrifices of Qi, Liang, and Chen had been cut off; Gao Renying, Xiao Cong, and Chen Shubao were ordered to perform sacrifices at the proper seasons; required implements would be supplied by the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the intercalary tenth month, on jiayin, an edict noted that the ancestral rites of Qi, Liang, and Chen had lapsed. Gao Renying, Xiao Cong, and Chen Shubao were ordered to perform the seasonal sacrifices, and the necessary ritual objects would be supplied by the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 陳叔寶從帝登邙山，侍飲，賦詩曰：「日月光天德，山河壯帝居；

translations.literal: Chen Shubao followed the emperor up Mount Mang, attended a drinking party, and composed a poem saying: "Sun and moon shine with Heaven's virtue; mountains and rivers strengthen the emperor's dwelling;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shubao accompanied the emperor up Mount Mang, attended a banquet, and composed a poem: "Sun and moon embody Heaven's virtue; mountains and rivers magnify the emperor's dwelling;

sentences.zh: 太平無以報，願上東封書。」

translations.literal: in peace I have no way to repay—may I submit a petition for the eastern feng and shan."
translations.idiomatic: in this age of peace I have no gift to offer—may I present a petition for the feng and shan rites at Mount Tai."

sentences.zh: 並表請封禪。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting the feng and shan.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a formal memorial requesting the feng and shan.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔答之。

translations.literal: The emperor answered with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 它日，復侍宴，及出，帝目之曰：「此敗豈不由酒！

translations.literal: Another day he again attended a banquet; as he left, the emperor eyed him and said: "Was this defeat not caused by wine!
translations.idiomatic: On another day Shubao again attended a banquet. As he left, the emperor watched him and said, "Wasn't your downfall caused by wine!

sentences.zh: 以作詩之功，何如思安時事！

translations.literal: With the merit of composing poems, how does it compare to thinking how to settle the affairs of the time!
translations.idiomatic: If you spent as much effort governing as you do composing poems, how much better off would you have been!

sentences.zh: 當賀若弼渡京口，彼人密啟告急，叔寶飲酒，遂不之省。

translations.literal: When He Ruo Bi crossed Jingkou, the men there secretly reported the emergency; Shubao was drinking wine and therefore did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ruo Bi crossed Jingkou, urgent dispatches arrived in secret, but Shubao was drinking and never even looked at them.

sentences.zh: 高熲至日，猶見啟在床下，未開封。

translations.literal: On the day Gao Jiong arrived, the reports were still seen under the bed, unopened.
translations.idiomatic: By the day Gao Jiong reached the capital, those dispatches were still under his bed, unopened.

sentences.zh: 此誠可笑，蓋天亡之也。

translations.literal: This is truly laughable—Heaven was simply destroying Chen.
translations.idiomatic: It is laughable, and yet Heaven had already doomed Chen.

sentences.zh: 昔苻氏征伐所得國，皆榮貴其主，苟欲求名，不知違天命；

translations.literal: In the past the Fu clan, in states obtained by conquest, all honored and enriched their rulers, seeking reputation without knowing they violated Heaven's mandate;
translations.idiomatic: When the Fu clan conquered states in the past, they honored the defeated rulers and enriched them, seeking a reputation for magnanimity without realizing they were defying Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 與之官，乃違天也。」

translations.literal: to give them office is to violate Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: To give such men office is to defy Heaven itself."

sentences.zh: 齊州刺史盧賁坐民饑閉民糶，除名。

translations.literal: Lu Bin, prefect of Qizhou, because during the people's famine he closed the people's grain sales, was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bin, prefect of Qizhou, was struck from the rolls for hoarding grain during the famine and refusing to sell to the people.

sentences.zh: 帝后復欲授以一州，賁對詔失旨，又有怨言，帝大怒，遂不用。

translations.literal: Later the emperor again wished to give him a prefecture; Bin answered the edict off the mark and also had complaints; the emperor was greatly angered and did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor wished to appoint him to another prefecture, but Bin answered the edict poorly and voiced complaints. The emperor was furious and refused to use him.

sentences.zh: 皇太子為言：「此輩並有佐命功，雖性行輕險，誠不可棄。」

translations.literal: The crown prince spoke for them: "These men all have merit in assisting the mandate; though their conduct is frivolous and dangerous, they truly should not be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince pleaded on their behalf: "These men all helped you seize the throne. Though their characters are reckless, you truly should not cast them aside."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我抑屈之，全其命也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have suppressed and bent them to preserve their lives.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have humbled them only to spare their lives.

sentences.zh: 微劉昉、鄭譯、盧賁、柳裘、皇甫績等，則我不至此。

translations.literal: But for Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, Lu Bin, Liu Qiu, Huangfu Ji, and the like, I would not have reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Without Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, Lu Bin, Liu Qiu, Huangfu Ji, and the rest, I would never have reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 然此等皆反覆子也，當周宣帝時，以無賴得幸。

translations.literal: Yet these are all men of shifting loyalty; in Emperor Xuan of Zhou's time they gained favor through rascality.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they are all faithless men who won favor in Emperor Xuan of Zhou's day through sheer audacity.

sentences.zh: 及帝大漸，顏之儀等請以趙王輔政，此輩行詐，顧命於我。

translations.literal: When the emperor was critically ill, Yan Zhiyi and others requested that the Prince of Zhao assist in government; these men practiced deceit and entrusted the mandate to me.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan lay dying, Yan Zhiyi and others wanted the Prince of Zhao to serve as regent, but these men schemed and placed the regency in my hands instead.

sentences.zh: 我將為政，又欲亂之，故昉謀大逆，譯為巫蠱。

translations.literal: When I was about to govern, they again wished to create disorder; hence Fang plotted great treason and Yi practiced witchcraft.
translations.idiomatic: Once I took power they tried to stir chaos again. Fang plotted treason, and Yi practiced witchcraft.

sentences.zh: 如賁之例，皆不滿志，任之則不遜，置之則怨望，自為難信，非我棄之。

translations.literal: Men like Bin were all dissatisfied in ambition; employed they were insubordinate, set aside they resented—by their own nature hard to trust; it is not that I abandoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Bin were never satisfied. Put them in office and they grew insolent; leave them aside and they nursed grievances. They made themselves impossible to trust. I did not cast them away—they cast themselves away.

sentences.zh: 眾人見此，謂我薄於功臣，斯不然矣。」

translations.literal: When the multitude sees this, they say I am stingy toward meritorious ministers—this is not so."
translations.idiomatic: People see this and say I am ungrateful to my founding supporters. That is not true."

sentences.zh: 賁遂廢，卒於家。

translations.literal: Bin was thus discarded and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was never employed again and died at home.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣帥百官抗表，固請封禪。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Guang led the hundred officials in submitting a memorial resisting and firmly requesting the feng and shan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guang of Jin led the hundred officials in memorializing repeatedly for the feng and shan rites.

sentences.zh: 帝令牛弘等創定儀注，既成，帝視之，曰：「茲事體大，朕何德以堪之！

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Niu Hong and others to create and fix the ritual regulations; when completed, the emperor viewed them and said: "This affair's body is great—what virtue have I to bear it!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Niu Hong and others to draft the ritual protocols. When they were finished, he reviewed them and said, "This rite is too grand for my modest virtue!

sentences.zh: 但當東巡，因致祭泰山耳。」

translations.literal: I should only tour east and thereby offer sacrifice at Mount Tai."
translations.idiomatic: I shall tour east and offer sacrifice at Mount Tai—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙未，車駕東巡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yiwei, the imperial carriage toured east.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yiwei, the emperor set out on an eastern tour.

sentences.zh: 上好禨祥小數，上儀同三司蕭吉上書曰：「甲寅，乙卯，天地之合也。

translations.literal: The emperor liked omens and minor numerology; the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equipage Xiao Ji submitted a memorial saying: "Jiayin and yimao are Heaven and Earth's union.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor delighted in omens and minor numerology. Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equipage Xiao Ji memorialized, "Jiayin and yimao mark the union of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 今茲甲寅之年，以辛酉朔旦冬至，來年乙卯，以甲子夏至。

translations.literal: In this jiayin year, on xinyou the new moon at winter solstice; next year yimao, on jiazi the summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This jiayin year brings winter solstice on the xinyou new moon, and next year's yimao year brings summer solstice on jiazi.

sentences.zh: 冬至陽始，郊天之日，即至尊本命；

translations.literal: Winter solstice is when yang begins; the day of suburban sacrifice to Heaven is precisely Your Majesty's birth year;
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice is when yang begins, and the day of suburban sacrifice to Heaven falls in Your Majesty's birth year;

sentences.zh: 夏至陰始，祀地之辰，即皇后本命。

translations.literal: summer solstice is when yin begins; the time of sacrifice to Earth is precisely the empress's birth year.
translations.idiomatic: summer solstice is when yin begins, and the day of sacrifice to Earth falls in the empress's birth year.

sentences.zh: 至尊德並乾之覆育，皇后仁同地之載養，所以二儀元氣並會本辰。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's virtue equals Qian's covering and nurturing; the empress's benevolence equals Earth's bearing and sustaining—therefore the primal qi of the two regulators both meet in their birth years."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue matches Heaven's nurturing power, and the empress's benevolence matches Earth's sustaining power. Thus the primal energies of the two regulators converge in your birth years."

sentences.zh: 上大悅，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed five hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and rewarded him with five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 吉，懿之孫也。

translations.literal: Ji was Yi's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was the grandson of Xiao Yi.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎侍郎王劭言上有龍顏戴干之表，指示群臣。

translations.literal: The Attendant Censor Wang Shao said the emperor had the dragon countenance and canopy-of-dryness appearance, and pointed it out to the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Wang Shao declared that the emperor bore the dragon countenance and canopy-of-dryness physiognomy, and pointed this out to the court.

sentences.zh: 上悅，拜著作郎。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and appointed him Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and appointed him Compiler in the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 劭前後上表言上受命符瑞甚眾，又采民間歌謠，引圖書讖緯，捃摭佛經，回易文字，曲加誣飾，撰《皇隋靈感志》三十卷奏之，上令宣示天下。

translations.literal: Shao before and after submitted memorials saying the emperor's receipt of the mandate had very many portents; he also gathered popular songs, cited charts, books, prophecies, and weft texts, culled Buddhist sutras, altered characters, bent and added false ornament, compiled thirty juan of Records of Imperial Sui Spiritual Responses and presented them; the emperor ordered them proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shao repeatedly memorialized about the many portents of the emperor's mandate. He collected folk songs, cited prophecy texts and weft charts, excerpted Buddhist scriptures, twisted characters, and embroidered the evidence into a thirty-juan work titled Records of Imperial Sui Spiritual Responses, which the emperor ordered proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 劭集諸州朝集，使盥手焚香，而讀之，曲折其聲，有如歌詠，經涉旬朔，遍而後罷。

translations.literal: Shao gathered the provincial assemblies at court, had them wash hands and burn incense, and read it; he bent his voice like song and chant; it took more than ten days and a month to finish throughout before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the provincial representatives at court, had them wash their hands and burn incense, and read the text aloud in a chanting voice. The recitation took more than a month to complete.

sentences.zh: 上益喜，前後賞賜優洽。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still more pleased; before and after rewards were generous and ample.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still more pleased and heaped rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬戌，車駕頓齊州。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renxu, the imperial carriage halted at Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renxu, the imperial procession halted at Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 庚午，為壇於泰山，柴燎祀天，以歲旱謝愆咎，禮如南郊；

translations.literal: On gengwu he made an altar on Mount Tai, burned firewood and offered sacrifice to Heaven to apologize for faults because of the year's drought; the ritual was like the southern suburbs;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he built an altar on Mount Tai, burned firewood, and sacrificed to Heaven to apologize for the drought, using the same rites as at the southern suburbs;

sentences.zh: 又親祀青帝壇。

translations.literal: he also personally sacrificed at the Green Emperor's altar.
translations.idiomatic: he also personally sacrificed at the altar of the Green Emperor.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: He pardoned the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙辰，收天下兵器，敢私造者坐之；

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingchen, he collected weapons throughout the realm; those who dared privately manufacture them would be punished;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingchen, he ordered all weapons in the realm confiscated. Private manufacture was punishable by law;

sentences.zh: 關中、緣邊不在其例。

translations.literal: Guanzhong and the border regions were not in this category.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong and the frontier regions were exempt.

sentences.zh: 三月，己未，至自東巡。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiwei, he returned from the eastern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiwei, he returned from the eastern tour.

sentences.zh: 仁壽宮成。

translations.literal: Renshou Palace was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Renshou Palace was completed.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，上幸仁壽宮。

translations.literal: On dinghai the emperor visited Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the emperor visited Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 時天暑，役夫死者相次於道，楊素悉焚除之。

translations.literal: At the time the weather was hot; corvée workers died one after another on the road; Yang Su had them all burned and removed.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was sweltering, and corvée workers were dying along the roads in succession. Yang Su had the bodies burned and cleared away.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，不悅。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及至，見制度壯麗，大怒曰：「楊素殫民力為離宮，為吾結怨天下。」

translations.literal: When he arrived and saw the regulations grand and magnificent, he raged: "Yang Su has exhausted the people's strength for a detached palace and has made resentment for me throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived and saw how grand the palace was, he raged, "Yang Su has exhausted the people's strength to build this pleasure palace and has made the whole realm resent me."

sentences.zh: 素聞之，惶恐，慮獲譴，以告封德彝。

translations.literal: When Su heard, he was fearful, worried he would be punished, and told Feng Deyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Su heard this he was terrified of punishment and confided in Feng Deyi.

sentences.zh: 曰：「公勿憂，俟皇后至，必有恩詔。」

translations.literal: He said: "Sir, do not worry—when the empress arrives, there will surely be a gracious edict."
translations.idiomatic: Feng said, "Do not worry. When the empress arrives there will surely be a gracious edict."

sentences.zh: 明日，上果召素入對，獨孤後勞之曰：「公知吾夫婦老，無以自娛，盛飾此宮，豈非忠孝！」

translations.literal: The next day the emperor indeed summoned Su for audience; Empress Dugu comforted him: "Sir, you know we husband and wife are old with no way to amuse ourselves—to splendidly adorn this palace—is this not loyalty and filial piety!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor summoned Su for an audience. Empress Dugu comforted him: "You know that we are old and have few pleasures. To adorn this palace so splendidly—is that not loyalty and filial piety?"

sentences.zh: 賜錢百萬，錦絹三千段。

translations.literal: She bestowed a million cash and three thousand bolts of brocade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: She rewarded him with a million cash and three thousand bolts of brocade and silk.

sentences.zh: 素負貴恃才，多所凌侮；

translations.literal: Su relied on his nobility and talent and often bullied others;
translations.idiomatic: Su relied on his rank and talent and often bullied others;

sentences.zh: 唯賞重德彝，每引之與論宰相職務，終日忘倦，因撫其床曰：「封郎必當據吾此座。」

translations.literal: only he prized and esteemed Deyi; each time he drew him to discuss chancellorial duties, forgetting weariness all day; he stroked his couch and said: "Master Feng will surely occupy this seat of mine."
translations.idiomatic: yet he prized Feng Deyi alone. He would draw him into discussions of chancellorial duties and talk all day without tiring, patting his couch and saying, "Master Feng will surely sit in this seat of mine one day."

sentences.zh: 屢薦於帝，帝擢為內史舍人。

translations.literal: He repeatedly recommended him to the emperor; the emperor promoted him to Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Feng repeatedly, and the emperor promoted him to Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己丑朔，赦天下。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the jichou new moon, he pardoned the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the jichou new moon, he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊子，詔鑿底柱。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuzi, an edict ordered cutting through the Bedrock Pillars.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuzi, an edict ordered the Bedrock Pillars cut through to improve navigation.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，相州刺史豆盧通貢綾文布，命焚之於朝堂。

translations.literal: On gengyin the prefect of Xiangzhou Doulu Tong presented patterned silk cloth as tribute; he was ordered to burn it in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Doulu Tong, prefect of Xiangzhou, presented patterned silk as tribute. The emperor ordered it burned in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，納言蘇威坐從祠太山不敬，免，俄而復位。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Director of the Secretariat Su Wei, because of irreverence while following the Mount Tai sacrifice, was dismissed, but soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Director of the Secretariat Su Wei was dismissed for irreverence during the Mount Tai sacrifice, but was soon restored to office.

sentences.zh: 上謂群臣曰：「世人言蘇威詐清，家累金玉，此妄言也。

translations.literal: The emperor told the ministers: "People say Su Wei feigns purity while his house is piled with gold and jade—this is false talk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "People say Su Wei only pretends to be upright while his house is piled with gold and jade. That is nonsense.

sentences.zh: 然其性狠戾，不切世要，求名太甚，從己則悅，違之必怒，此其大病耳。」

translations.literal: Yet his nature is fierce and perverse, not attuned to the age's needs, seeking fame too greatly; if one follows him he is pleased, if one opposes he must rage—this is his great illness."
translations.idiomatic: But his nature is harsh and obstinate, out of touch with practical affairs, and too hungry for reputation. Agree with him and he is delighted; cross him and he flies into a rage. That is his real flaw."

sentences.zh: 戊寅，上至自仁壽宮。

translations.literal: On wuyin the emperor returned from Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the emperor returned from Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊子，以吏部尚書韋世康為荊州總管。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuzi, he appointed Wei Shikang, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, as overall commander of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuzi he made Wei Shikang, Minister of Personnel, overall commander of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 世康，洸之弟也，和靜謙恕，在吏部十餘年，時稱廉平。

translations.literal: Shikang was Guang's younger brother—harmonious, quiet, modest, and forgiving; he served in the Ministry of Personnel for more than ten years and was at the time called honest and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang was the younger brother of Wei Guang—gentle, quiet, modest, and forgiving. He had served in the Ministry of Personnel for more than ten years and was known for integrity and fairness.

sentences.zh: 常有止足之志，謂子弟曰：「祿豈須多，防滿則退；

translations.literal: He often held the resolve to know when to stop, telling his sons and younger brothers: "Need salary be abundant? Guard against fullness and withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: He often spoke of knowing when he had enough, telling his family, "Why must one's salary be great? When you have enough, step back;

sentences.zh: 年不待暮，有疾便辭。」

translations.literal: do not wait until old age; if illness comes, resign at once."
translations.idiomatic: Do not wait until you are old; resign at the first sign of illness."

sentences.zh: 因懇乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Thereupon he earnestly begged permission to retire with his old bones.
translations.idiomatic: He then earnestly petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，使鎮荊州。

translations.literal: The emperor did not approve but sent him to govern Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused but sent him to govern Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時天下惟有四總管，並、揚、益、荊，以晉、秦、蜀三王及世康為之，當世以為榮。

translations.literal: At the time throughout the realm there were only four overall commanders—Bing, Yang, Yi, and Jing; the three princes of Jin, Qin, and Shu, together with Shikang, held these posts—a glory in that age.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were only four regional overall commanders in the realm—Bing, Yang, Yi, and Jing. The three princes of Jin, Qin, and Shu, together with Shikang, held these posts, and the age regarded it as a supreme honor.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛酉，上幸溫湯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinyou, the emperor visited the hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinyou, the emperor visited the hot springs.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊子，敕：「盜邊糧一升已上，皆斬，仍籍沒其家。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuzi, an edict: "Those who steal border grain, one sheng or more, shall all be decapitated, and their households still registered and confiscated."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuzi, an edict declared: "Anyone who steals a sheng or more of frontier grain will be beheaded, and the offender's household will be registered and confiscated."

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔文武官以四考受代。

translations.literal: On jichou an edict ordered civil and military officials to yield their posts after four evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou an edict required civil and military officials to surrender their posts after four performance reviews.

sentences.zh: 汴州刺史令狐熙來朝，考績為天下之最，賜帛三百匹，頒告天下。

translations.literal: Linghu Xi, prefect of Bianzhou, came to court; his examination record ranked highest in the realm; he was granted three hundred bolts of silk and the matter proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Xi, prefect of Bianzhou, came to court. His performance review ranked first in the realm, and he was granted three hundred bolts of silk; the achievement was proclaimed throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 熙，整之子也。

translations.literal: Xi was Zheng's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was the son of Linghu Zheng.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁亥，以皇孫裕為平原王，筠為安成王，嶷為安平王，恪為襄城王，該為高陽王，韶為建安王，煚為穎川王，皆勇之子也。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dinghai, he enfeoffed the emperor's grandsons Yu as Prince of Pingyuan, Yun as Prince of Ancheng, Ni as Prince of Anping, Ke as Prince of Xiangcheng, Gai as Prince of Gaoyang, Shao as Prince of Jian'an, and Jiong as Prince of Yingchuan—all sons of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dinghai the emperor enfeoffed his grandsons: Yu as Prince of Pingyuan, Yun as Prince of Ancheng, Ni as Prince of Anping, Ke as Prince of Xiangcheng, Gai as Prince of Gaoyang, Shao as Prince of Jian'an, and Jiong as Prince of Yingchuan—all sons of Prince Yong.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，甲午，初制工商不得仕進。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, on jiawu, for the first time a regulation barred merchants and artisans from entering official service.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, on jiawu a new rule barred merchants and artisans from official careers.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，丙戌，詔：「決死罪者，三奏然後行刑。」

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on bingxu, an edict: "For those sentenced to death, after three reports only then carry out execution."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on bingxu an edict declared: "Before carrying out a death sentence, the case must be reported three times."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己丑，上幸長春宮；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jichou, the emperor visited Changchun Palace;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jichou the emperor visited Changchun Palace;

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬子，還長安。

translations.literal: in the eleventh month, on renzi, he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: in the eleventh month, on renzi, he returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 党項寇會州，詔發隴西兵討降之。

translations.literal: The Tangut raided Huizhou; an edict dispatched Longxi troops to attack and reduce them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut attacked Huizhou, and an edict dispatched troops from Longxi to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 帝以光化公主妻吐谷渾可汗世伏；

translations.literal: The emperor gave Princess Guanghua in marriage to Shifu, khan of the Tuyuhun;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Princess Guanghua in marriage to Shifu, khan of the Tuyuhun;

sentences.zh: 世伏上表請稱公主為天後，上不許。

translations.literal: Shifu memorialized asking to call the princess Heavenly Empress; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shifu submitted a memorial asking to address the princess as Heavenly Empress, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，癸未，太平公史萬歲擊南寧羌，平之。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on guiwei, Duke of Taiping Shi Wansui attacked the Nanning Qiang and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on guiwei Duke of Taiping Shi Wansui attacked the Nanning tribes and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 初，梁睿之克王謙也，西南夷、獠莫不歸附，唯南寧州酋帥爨震恃遠不服。

translations.literal: Initially, when Liang Rui conquered Wang Qian, the southwestern Yi and Liao all submitted—only Cuan Zhen, chieftain of Nanning Prefecture, relying on distance, did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Rui earlier conquered Wang Qian, the tribes of the southwest all submitted—only Cuan Zhen, chieftain of Nanning, held out in his remote territory.

sentences.zh: 睿上疏，以為：「南寧州，漢世牂柯之地，戶口殷眾，金寶富饒。

translations.literal: Rui memorialized, arguing: "Nanning Prefecture is the land of Zangke in Han times—its population is abundant and its gold and treasure rich.
translations.idiomatic: Rui submitted a memorial arguing that Nanning had been Zangke territory in Han times, with a large population and rich stores of gold and treasure.

sentences.zh: 梁南寧州刺史徐文盛為湘東王征赴荊州，屬東夏尚阻，未遑遠略，土民爨瓚遂竊據一方，國家遙授刺史，其子震相承至今。

translations.literal: Xu Wensheng, Liang prefect of Nanning, was summoned by the Prince of Xiangdong to go to Jingzhou; as the eastern lands were still obstructed and distant schemes had no place, the local people—Cuan Zan—seized a region for himself; the state remotely invested him as prefect, and his son Zhen has inherited the post down to today.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liang, Nanning prefect Xu Wensheng was summoned by the Prince of Xiangdong to Jingzhou. While eastern affairs still commanded attention, the court had no leisure for distant campaigns, and the local leader Cuan Zan seized the region. The state invested him as prefect from afar, and his son Zhen has held the post ever since.

sentences.zh: 而震臣禮多虧，貢賦不入，乞因平蜀之眾，略定南寧。」

translations.literal: Yet Zhen's observance of ministerial rites is much deficient and tribute and taxes do not enter; I beg, using the forces that pacified Shu, to bring Nanning roughly to order."
translations.idiomatic: But Zhen is lax in feudal obligations and sends no tribute or taxes. I ask permission to use the army that pacified Shu to subdue Nanning as well."

sentences.zh: 其後南寧夷爨玩來降，拜昆州刺史，既而復叛。

translations.literal: Later the Nanning Yi Cuan Wan came to surrender and was appointed prefect of Kunzhou, but soon rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Nanning chieftain Cuan Wan surrendered and was appointed prefect of Kunzhou, but soon rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 乃以左領軍將軍史萬歲為行軍總管，帥眾擊之，入自蜻蛉川，至於南中。

translations.literal: Shi Wansui, General of the Left Guard, was made campaign commander and led troops against him, entering by Qingling Stream and reaching the southern interior.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wansui, General of the Left Guard, was appointed campaign commander and marched against him, entering through Qingling Stream into the southern interior.

sentences.zh: 夷人前後屯據要害，萬歲皆擊破之；

translations.literal: The Yi in succession held strategic passes; Wansui attacked and broke them all;
translations.idiomatic: The tribes held the strategic passes one after another, and Wansui broke through them all;

sentences.zh: 過諸葛亮紀功碑，渡西洱河，入渠濫川，行千餘里，破其三十餘部，虜獲男女二萬餘口。

translations.literal: passed Zhuge Liang's memorial stele, crossed the Western Er River, entered Qulan Stream, traveled more than a thousand li, broke more than thirty of their divisions, and captured men and women numbering more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He passed Zhuge Liang's victory stele, crossed the Western Er River, and entered Qulan Stream. After marching more than a thousand li, he broke more than thirty tribal divisions and took more than twenty thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 諸夷大懼，遣使請降，獻明珠徑寸，於是勒石頌美隋德。

translations.literal: The various Yi were greatly afraid, sent envoys to request surrender, and presented pearls an inch across; thereupon a stone was carved praising Sui virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were terrified. They sent envoys to surrender and presented pearls an inch in diameter. Wansui had a stele carved praising the virtue of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 萬歲請將爨玩入朝，詔許之。

translations.literal: Wansui requested to bring Cuan Wan to court; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wansui asked to bring Cuan Wan to court, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 爨玩陰有二心，不欲詣闕，賂萬歲以金寶，萬歲於是捨玩而還。

translations.literal: Cuan Wan secretly had a divided heart and did not wish to go to the capital; he bribed Wansui with gold and treasure, and Wansui therefore left Wan behind and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Cuan Wan had no intention of going to court. He secretly bribed Wansui with gold and jewels, and Wansui left him behind and returned.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，上幸仁壽宮。

translations.literal: On gengyin the emperor visited Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the emperor visited Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 桂州俚帥李光仕作亂，帝遣上柱國王世積與前桂州總管周法尚討之，法尚發嶺南兵，世積發嶺北兵，俱會尹州。

translations.literal: Li Guangshi, Li chieftain of Guizhou, rebelled; the emperor sent Senior Statesman Wang Shiji and former overall commander of Guizhou Zhou Fashang to suppress him; Fashang mobilized troops south of the mountains, Shiji mobilized troops north of the mountains, and both assembled at Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangshi, a Li chieftain in Guizhou, rebelled. The emperor sent Senior Statesman Wang Shiji and former Guizhou commander Zhou Fashang against him. Fashang raised troops south of the Nanling passes, Shiji raised troops north of them, and both converged on Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 世積所部遇瘴，不能進，頓於衡州，法尚獨討之。

translations.literal: Shiji's division encountered miasma and could not advance, halting at Hengzhou; Fashang alone pursued the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji's troops were halted by miasma in Hengzhou and could not advance. Fashang continued the campaign alone.

sentences.zh: 光仕戰敗，帥勁兵走保白石洞。

translations.literal: Guangshi was defeated in battle and led picked troops to flee and hold Bai Rock Cave.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi was defeated and fled with his best troops to hold Bai Rock Cave.

sentences.zh: 法尚大獲家口，其黨有來降者，輒以妻子還之。

translations.literal: Fashang captured many families; when his followers came to surrender, he immediately returned their wives and children to them.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang captured many families. Whenever a follower surrendered, he immediately returned the man's wife and children.

sentences.zh: 居旬日，降者數千人。

translations.literal: Within ten days, those who surrendered numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days several thousand men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 光仕眾潰而走，追斬之。

translations.literal: Guangshi's host scattered and fled; they pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi's force collapsed and fled; pursuers caught and killed him.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣員外散騎侍郎何稠募兵討光仕，稠諭降其黨莫崇等，承製署首領為州縣官。

translations.literal: The emperor also sent Supernumerary Palace Secretariat Attendant He Chou to raise troops against Guangshi; Chou persuaded Guangshi's followers Mo Chong and others to surrender and, by imperial order, appointed chieftains as prefectural and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Supernumerary Palace Attendant He Chou to raise troops. Chou persuaded followers such as Mo Chong to surrender and, by imperial commission, appointed tribal leaders as prefectural and county officials.

sentences.zh: 稠，妥之兄子也。

translations.literal: Chou was the son of Tuo's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chou was the nephew of He Tuo.

sentences.zh: 上以嶺南夷、越數反，以汴州刺史令狐熙為桂州總管十七州諸軍事，許以便宜從事，刺史以下官得承製補授。

translations.literal: Because the Yi and Yue of Lingnan repeatedly rebelled, the emperor appointed Linghu Xi, prefect of Bianzhou, overall commander of military affairs for seventeen prefectures of Guizhou, permitting discretionary action; officials below prefect might be appointed and supplemented by imperial order.
