translations.idiomatic: Because the tribes of Lingnan rebelled repeatedly, the emperor appointed Linghu Xi, prefect of Bianzhou, commander over seventeen Guizhou prefectures with full discretionary authority, including power to appoint officials below the rank of prefect by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 熙至部，大弘恩信，其溪洞渠帥更相謂曰：「前時總管皆以兵威相脅，今者乃以手教相諭，我輩其可違乎！」

translations.literal: When Xi reached his post he greatly spread grace and trust; the chieftains of the stream valleys and caves said to one another: "Former overall commanders all coerced us with military might; now he instructs us with handwritten orders—how can we disobey!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xi reached his post, he relied on grace and good faith. The chieftains of the valleys said to one another, "Previous commanders threatened us with armed force, but this one appeals to us with his own letters. How can we refuse?"

sentences.zh: 於是相帥歸附。

translations.literal: Thereupon they led one another in submission.
translations.idiomatic: They then submitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 先是州縣生梗，長吏多不得之官，寄政於總管府。

translations.literal: Previously the prefectures and counties were stubborn; chief officials often could not reach their posts, and government was entrusted to the overall commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the prefectures and counties had been ungovernable, and many appointed magistrates never reached their posts; administration was handled from the commander's office.

sentences.zh: 熙悉遣之，為建城邑，開設學校，華、夷感化焉。

translations.literal: Xi sent them all out, built cities and towns, and established schools; Chinese and Yi were moved by his influence.
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent officials to every post, built towns, and established schools. Both Chinese settlers and native peoples were won over.

sentences.zh: 俚帥寧猛力，在陳世已據南海，隋因而撫之，拜安州刺史。

translations.literal: Ning Mengli, a Li chieftain, had already held the South Sea under the Chen; the Sui accordingly mollified him and appointed him prefect of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Li chieftain Ning Mengli had held the South Sea region under the Chen. The Sui court conciliated him and appointed him prefect of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 猛力恃險驕倨，未嘗參謁。

translations.literal: Mengli relied on dangerous terrain and was proud and insolent, never attending audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Mengli relied on his rugged territory and never came to pay respects—proud and defiant.

sentences.zh: 熙諭以恩信，猛力感之，詣府請謁，不敢為非。

translations.literal: Xi instructed him with grace and trust; Mengli was moved, came to the headquarters to request audience, and dared not do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi won him over with kindness and trust. Mengli was moved, came to headquarters to pay his respects, and afterward dared not cause trouble.

sentences.zh: 熙奏改安州為欽州。

translations.literal: Xi memorialized to change Anzhou to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi memorialized to rename Anzhou as Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝以所在屬官不敬憚其上，事難克舉，三月，丙辰，詔「諸司論屬官罪，有律輕情重者，聽於律外斟酌決杖。」

translations.literal: The emperor, because subordinate officials everywhere did not respect and fear their superiors and affairs were hard to accomplish, in the third month on bingchen issued an edict: "When offices discuss subordinates' crimes, if the law is light but the circumstances heavy, they may outside the law weigh and decide flogging."
translations.idiomatic: Because subordinate officials everywhere showed no respect for their superiors and government work suffered, in the third month on bingchen the emperor issued an edict: "When judging subordinates' crimes, if the statute is lenient but the offense serious, superiors may impose flogging beyond what the law allows."

sentences.zh: 於是上下相驅，迭行捶楚，以殘暴為干能，以守法為懦弱。

translations.literal: Thereupon superiors and subordinates drove one another, alternately applying beating and flogging; cruelty was taken as competence, and observance of law as weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at every level took this as license to beat their subordinates. Cruelty passed for competence; fidelity to the law was mocked as weakness.

sentences.zh: 帝以盜賊繁多，命盜一錢以上皆棄市，或三人共盜一瓜，事發即死。

translations.literal: Because bandits and thieves were numerous, the emperor ordered that theft of one cash or more all be executed in the marketplace, or if three men together stole one melon—once the matter surfaced, immediate death.
translations.idiomatic: With theft rampant, the emperor decreed death for stealing as little as one cash—or for three men sharing a stolen melon. Offenders were executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 於是行旅皆晏起早宿，天下懍懍。

translations.literal: Thereupon travelers all set out late and lodged early; the realm was fearful and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers dared venture out only late in the day and lodge early; fear spread across the realm.

sentences.zh: 有數人劫執事而謂之曰：「吾豈求財者邪！

translations.literal: Several men seized an attendant and said to him: "Am I one who seeks wealth!
translations.idiomatic: Several men seized a court attendant and said, "Do you think we are common thieves?

sentences.zh: 但為枉人來耳。

translations.literal: I have come only on behalf of a wronged man.
translations.idiomatic: We came only to speak for the wronged.

sentences.zh: 而為我奏至尊：自古以來，體國立法，未有盜一錢而死者也。

translations.literal: Yet report to the Supreme Sovereign for me: since antiquity, in establishing the state and making law, never has one who stole one cash been put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Report to His Majesty for us: since antiquity, no state has made death the penalty for stealing a single cash.

sentences.zh: 而不為我以聞，吾更來，而屬無類矣！」

translations.literal: If you do not report this for me, I shall come again—and then there will be none of your sort left!"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not carry our words to him, we will come again—and then people like you will not survive!"

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，為停此法。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he stopped this law.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he abolished the law.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗乘怒，欲以六月杖殺人，大理少卿河東趙綽固爭曰：「季夏之月，天地成長庶類，不可以此時誅殺。」

translations.literal: Once the emperor, seized by anger, wished in the sixth month to beat someone to death; Zhao Chuo of Hedong, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, firmly remonstrated: "In the last month of summer, Heaven and Earth bring all living things to growth—it is not permissible to execute and kill at this time."
translations.idiomatic: Once, in a fit of anger during the sixth month, the emperor wished to beat a man to death. Zhao Chuo of Hedong, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, firmly remonstrated: "In midsummer, when Heaven and Earth nurture all living things, executions are forbidden."

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「六月雖曰生長，此時必有雷霆；

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "Though the sixth month is called a time of growth, at this season there are always thunderclaps;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Summer may be a season of growth, but thunder still rolls at this time of year;

sentences.zh: 我則天而行，有何不可！」

translations.literal: I act in accord with Heaven—what may not be done!"
translations.idiomatic: I act as Heaven does. What may I not do?"

sentences.zh: 遂殺之。

translations.literal: He then had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: And he had the man beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 大理掌固來曠上言大理官司太寬，帝以曠為忠直，遣每旦於五品行中參見。

translations.literal: Lai Kuang, a clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, submitted that the court's judgments were too lenient; the emperor deemed Kuang loyal and straight and had him attend morning audiences among officials of the fifth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Kuang, a clerk in the Court of Judicial Review, complained that the court was too lenient. The emperor judged him loyal and direct and ordered him to attend the morning assembly with officials of the fifth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 曠又告少卿趙綽濫免徒囚，帝使信臣推驗，初無阿曲，帝怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: Kuang also accused Vice Director Zhao Chuo of improperly releasing bonded convicts; the emperor had trusted ministers investigate and verify; at first there was no favoritism found; the emperor grew angry and ordered Kuang executed.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang also accused Zhao Chuo of improperly releasing convicts. The emperor sent trusted officials to investigate and found no favoritism—but flew into a rage and ordered Kuang executed.

sentences.zh: 綽固爭，以為曠不合死，帝拂衣入閣。

translations.literal: Chuo firmly remonstrated, holding that Kuang did not deserve death; the emperor swept his robes and entered the inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo insisted that Kuang did not deserve death. The emperor swept aside his robes and stalked into the inner chamber.

sentences.zh: 綽矯言，「臣更不理曠，自有它事，未及奏聞。」

translations.literal: Chuo falsely said, "Your servant will no longer handle Kuang's case; there is another matter I have not yet reported."
translations.idiomatic: Chuo said falsely, "Your Majesty, I am no longer concerned with Kuang's case. There is another matter I have not yet reported."

sentences.zh: 帝命引入閣，綽再拜請曰：「臣有死罪三，臣為大理少卿，不能制馭掌固，使曠觸掛天刑，一也。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him brought into the inner chamber; Chuo bowed again and pleaded: "Your servant has three crimes deserving death: first, as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review I could not control the clerks and allowed Kuang to incur imperial punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him brought in. Chuo bowed and said, "Your servant is guilty of three capital offenses. First, as Vice Director I failed to control my clerks and allowed Kuang to offend against imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 囚不合死，而臣不能死爭，二也。

translations.literal: The prisoner did not deserve death, yet I could not remonstrate to the death—second.
translations.idiomatic: Second, Kuang did not deserve death, yet I failed to remonstrate as if my life depended on it.

sentences.zh: 臣本無它事，而妄言求入，三也。」

translations.literal: I originally had no other matter, yet spoke falsely to gain entry—third."
translations.idiomatic: Third, I had no other business but lied to gain audience with Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝解顏。

translations.literal: The emperor's expression relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face softened.

sentences.zh: 會獨孤後在坐，命賜綽二金盃酒，並杯賜之。

translations.literal: Empress Dugu happened to be present; he ordered two gold cups of wine given to Chuo, and had both cups bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu was present. The emperor ordered two gold cups of wine for Chuo and had both cups given to him.

sentences.zh: 曠因免死，徙廣州。

translations.literal: Kuang was thereby spared death and was exiled to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang was spared and exiled to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 蕭摩訶子世略在江南作亂，摩訶當從坐，上曰：「世略年未二十，亦何能為？

translations.literal: Xiao Mohe's son Shilue raised rebellion in Jiangnan; Mohe was liable to punishment by association; the emperor said: "Shilue is not yet twenty—what could he accomplish?
translations.idiomatic: Shilue, son of Xiao Mohe, rebelled in the south. Mohe faced punishment by association. The emperor said, "Shilue is not yet twenty. What could he possibly have done?

sentences.zh: 以其名將之子，為人所逼耳。」

translations.literal: As the son of a famous general, he was compelled by others—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a famous general, he was driven to it by others."

sentences.zh: 因赦摩訶。

translations.literal: He therefore pardoned Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: He then pardoned Mohe.

sentences.zh: 綽固諫不可，上不能奪，欲綽去而赦之，因命綽退食。

translations.literal: Chuo firmly remonstrated that this could not be; the emperor could not overcome him; wishing Chuo to leave and then pardon Mohe, he therefore ordered Chuo to withdraw for his meal.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo firmly objected. The emperor could not prevail and, wanting Chuo gone before pardoning Mohe, ordered him to withdraw for his meal.

sentences.zh: 綽曰：「臣奏獄未決，不敢退。」

translations.literal: Chuo said: "Your servant's case is undecided—I dare not withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Chuo said, "The case is not yet decided. I dare not withdraw."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「大理其為朕特捨摩訶也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Court of Judicial Review, make a special exception for Me and spare Mohe."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Court of Judicial Review, grant Me a special exception and spare Mohe."

sentences.zh: 因命左右釋之。

translations.literal: He then ordered attendants to release him.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered attendants to release Mohe.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎辛但嘗衣緋褌，俗雲利官；

translations.literal: Xin Dan, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, once wore red drawers; common talk said this brought official advancement;
translations.idiomatic: Xin Dan, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, once wore red undergarments—a folk superstition said this brought promotion;

sentences.zh: 上以為厭蠱，將斬之。

translations.literal: the emperor regarded it as sorcery against harm and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor took this for witchcraft and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 綽曰：「法不當死，臣不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Chuo said: "By law he does not deserve death—I dare not obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Chuo said, "The law does not prescribe death. I dare not obey."

sentences.zh: 上怒甚，曰：「卿惜辛但而不自惜也！」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and said: "You spare Xin Dan and do not spare yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. "You would spare Xin Dan but not yourself!"

sentences.zh: 命引綽斬之。

translations.literal: He ordered Chuo led out to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Chuo led out for execution.

sentences.zh: 綽曰：「陛下寧殺臣，不可殺辛但。」

translations.literal: Chuo said: "Your Majesty may better kill your servant—you cannot kill Xin Dan."
translations.idiomatic: Chuo said, "Your Majesty may kill me, but you may not kill Xin Dan."

sentences.zh: 至朝堂，解衣當斬，上使人謂綽曰：「竟何如？」

translations.literal: When they reached the court hall, he removed his robe to await execution; the emperor sent someone to say to Chuo: "How is it in the end?"
translations.idiomatic: At the execution ground Chuo stripped for the axe. The emperor sent a messenger: "What do you say now?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「執法一心，不敢惜死！」

translations.literal: He replied: "Upholding the law with one heart—I dare not spare my life!"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I uphold the law with all my heart and do not fear death!"

sentences.zh: 上拂衣而入，良久，乃釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor swept his robes and went inside; after a long while, he then released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned away and went inside. After a long while he ordered Chuo released.

sentences.zh: 明日謝綽，勞勉之，賜物三百段。

translations.literal: The next day he apologized to Chuo, commended and encouraged him, and bestowed three hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor apologized to Chuo, praised his steadfastness, and rewarded him with three hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 時上禁行惡錢，有二人在市，以惡錢易好者，武候執以聞，上令悉斬之，綽進諫曰：「此人所坐當杖，殺之非法。」

translations.literal: At the time the emperor forbade circulating debased coin; two men in the market exchanged debased coin for good coin; guard officers seized them and reported; the emperor ordered all beheaded; Chuo stepped forward to remonstrate: "What these men are guilty of deserves the rod—to kill them is against the law."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor had banned debased coin. Two men in the market traded bad coin for good; guards seized them and reported. The emperor ordered both beheaded. Chuo remonstrated: "Their offense merits flogging, not execution."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不關卿事。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This does not concern you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is none of your affair."

sentences.zh: 綽曰：「陛下不以臣愚闇，置在法司，欲妄殺人，豈得不關臣事！」

translations.literal: Chuo said: "Your Majesty, not deeming your servant stupid and dark, placed me in the legal office—if you wish to kill people recklessly, how can it not concern your servant's affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: Chuo said, "Your Majesty did not think me too dull to appoint me to the court of law. If you intend to kill men unlawfully, how can that be none of my affair?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「撼大木，不動者當退。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When shaking a great tree, one who does not move should withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When you shake a great tree, the branch that will not bend should be cut away."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣望感天心，何論動木。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant hopes to move the heart of Heaven—what talk of moving trees!"
translations.idiomatic: Chuo replied, "I hope to move the heart of Heaven itself. What talk of moving trees?"

sentences.zh: 上復曰：「啜羹者熱則置之，天子之威，欲相挫邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor again said: "One who sips soup, when it is hot, sets it aside—the Son of Heaven's authority: do you wish to wear it down!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied again, "When soup is too hot, one sets it aside. Do you mean to blunt the Son of Heaven's authority?

sentences.zh: 綽拜而益前，訶之，不肯退，上遂入。

translations.literal: Chuo bowed and pressed forward still more; the emperor berated him, but he would not withdraw, and the emperor thereupon went inside.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo bowed and stepped even closer. The emperor shouted at him, but he would not retreat, and the emperor finally went inside.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史柳彧復上奏切諫，上乃止。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary of the Secretariat Liu Yu again submitted a memorial strongly remonstrating, and the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Yu submitted another forceful memorial, and the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 上以綽有誠直之心，每引入閣中，或遇上與皇后同榻，即呼綽坐，評論得失，前後賞賜萬計。

translations.literal: Because the emperor saw that Chuo had a sincere and upright heart, he often brought him into the inner pavilion; sometimes when he encountered the emperor and empress sharing a couch, he would summon Chuo to sit and discuss gains and losses; rewards before and after numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Chuo sincere and upright, the emperor often summoned him to the inner chambers. At times when he and the empress were on the same couch, he would call Chuo to sit with them and discuss affairs of state. Over time he lavished on Chuo rewards beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 與大理卿薛冑同時，俱名平恕；

translations.literal: At the same time as Director of the Court of Justice Xue Zhou, both were famed for fairness and clemency;
translations.idiomatic: In the same era as Xue Zhou, Director of the Court of Justice, both men were famed for fairness and clemency—

sentences.zh: 然冑斷獄以情而綽守法，俱為稱職。

translations.literal: Yet Zhou judged cases by sentiment while Chuo upheld the law—both were equally fit for their offices.
translations.idiomatic: yet Zhou decided cases with an eye to human circumstances while Chuo held strictly to the law. Both were regarded as fully equal to their duties.

sentences.zh: 冑，端之子也。

translations.literal: Zhou was the son of Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was the son of Duan.

sentences.zh: 帝晚節用法益峻，御史於元日不劾武官衣劍之不齊者，帝曰：「爾為御史，縱捨自由。」

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor applied the law with growing severity. On New Year's Day a censor did not impeach military officers whose dress and swords were not in order. The emperor said: "You serve as censor yet freely pass over offenses."
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor grew ever harsher in enforcing the law. On New Year's Day a censor failed to impeach military officers whose dress and swords were out of order. The emperor said, "You are a censor, yet you let offenses pass as you please."

sentences.zh: 命殺之，諫議大夫毛思祖諫，又殺之。

translations.literal: He ordered the censor killed. Remonstrance and Advice Grandee Mao Sizu remonstrated—and he was killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the censor executed. Remonstrance and Advice Grandee Mao Sizu protested—and was executed too.

sentences.zh: 將作寺丞以課麥遲晚，武庫令以署庭荒蕪，左右出使，或授牧宰馬鞭、鸚鵡，帝察知，並親臨斬之。

translations.literal: A Director of Palace Construction's assistant was beheaded for turning in his wheat quota late; an Armory Director for letting his office courtyard go to weed; attendants on missions abroad who gave district magistrates horsewhips or parrots—the emperor discovered these and personally executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: A deputy of the Directorate of Palace Construction was beheaded because his wheat quota was late. The Director of the Armory was beheaded because his office yard had gone to weeds. Attendants on foreign missions who gave local magistrates horsewhips or parrots—when the emperor learned of it, he personally executed them all.

sentences.zh: 帝既喜怒不恆，不復依準科律。

translations.literal: The emperor's joy and anger being no longer constant, he no longer adhered to the statutes and laws.
translations.idiomatic: His moods now swung wildly, and he no longer governed by the code of law.

sentences.zh: 信任楊素，素復任情不平，與鴻臚少卿陳延有隙，嘗經蕃客館，庭中以馬屎，又眾僕於氈上樗蒲，以白帝。

translations.literal: He trusted Yang Su; Su again indulged his feelings unjustly. He had a grudge against Vice Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception Chen Yan. Once passing the foreign guests' lodge, he found horse dung in the courtyard and many servants gambling on felt mats, and reported this to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted Yang Su, who again ruled by whim rather than justice. Su bore a grudge against Vice Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception Chen Yan. Passing the lodge for foreign guests one day, he found horse dung in the courtyard and servants gambling on felt mats, and reported it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，主客令及樗蒲者皆杖殺之，棰陳延幾死。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged; the Master of Reception and the gamblers were all beaten to death; Chen Yan was thrashed nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage. The Master of Reception and the gamblers were all beaten to death. Chen Yan was flogged almost to death.

sentences.zh: 帝遣新衛大都督長安屈突通往隴西檢覆群牧，得隱匿馬二萬餘匹，帝大怒，將斬太僕卿慕容悉達及諸監官千五百人。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the new guards grand commander of Chang'an, Qutu Tong, to Longxi to inspect the horse pastures and found more than twenty thousand hidden horses. The emperor was greatly enraged and was about to execute Grand Master of Studs Murong Xida and fifteen hundred supervising officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Qutu Tong, the new guard commander at Chang'an, to Longxi to inspect the imperial pastures. More than twenty thousand concealed horses were discovered. In a fury the emperor prepared to execute Grand Master of Studs Murong Xida and fifteen hundred pasture officials.

sentences.zh: 通諫曰：「人命至重，陛下奈何以畜產之故殺千有餘人！

translations.literal: Tong remonstrated: "Human life is supremely weighty—how can Your Majesty for the sake of livestock kill more than a thousand people!
translations.idiomatic: Tong remonstrated, "Human life is beyond price. How can Your Majesty slaughter more than a thousand men over livestock!

sentences.zh: 臣敢以死請！」

translations.literal: Your servant dares petition with his life!"
translations.idiomatic: I dare ask for their lives at the cost of my own!"

sentences.zh: 帝□真目叱之，通又頓首曰：「臣一身份死，就陛下丐千餘人命。」

translations.literal: The emperor glared and shouted at him. Tong again prostrated himself and said: "Your servant offers one body to die—before Your Majesty I beg the lives of more than a thousand men."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor glared and shouted him down. Tong prostrated himself again. "Let this one body die—I beg Your Majesty for the lives of those thousand men."

sentences.zh: 帝感寤，曰：「朕之不明，以至於此！

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to awakening and said: "My lack of clarity has reached this point!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved to his senses. "How could my judgment have fallen so low!

sentences.zh: 賴有卿忠言耳。」

translations.literal: It is thanks to your loyal words alone."
translations.idiomatic: I owe it only to your loyal counsel."

sentences.zh: 於是悉達等皆減死論，擢通為右武候將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xida and the rest were all sentenced with death reduced, and Tong was promoted to General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xida and the others were all spared execution, and Tong was promoted to General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 上柱國彭公劉昶與帝有舊，帝甚親之；

translations.literal: Grand General Duke of Peng Liu Chang had old ties with the emperor, and the emperor was very close to him;
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Liu Chang, Duke of Peng, was an old companion of the emperor, who held him in great affection—

sentences.zh: 其子居士，任俠不遵法度，數有罪，上以昶故，每原之。

translations.literal: His son Jushi was chivalrous and heedless of law, repeatedly guilty of crimes; because of Chang the emperor always pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jushi was a swaggering freebooter who scorned the law and repeatedly broke it. Out of regard for Chang, the emperor always pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 居士轉驕恣，取公卿子弟雄健者，輒將至家，以車輪括其頸而棒之，殆死能不屈者，稱為壯士，釋而與交。

translations.literal: Jushi grew ever more arrogant. He would take stalwart sons of high ministers and bring them home, put a cart wheel around their necks and beat them with clubs; those who nearly died yet would not yield he called brave men, released them, and befriended them.
translations.idiomatic: Jushi grew ever bolder. He would seize strong sons of high officials, bring them home, loop a cart wheel around their necks, and beat them with clubs. Any who nearly died rather than submit he hailed as true men, freed, and took as companions.

sentences.zh: 黨與三百人，毆擊路人，多所侵奪，至於公卿妃主，莫敢與校。

translations.literal: With a gang of three hundred he beat passersby and seized much by force; even the consorts and princesses of high ministers—none dared contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: His band numbered three hundred. They assaulted wayfarers and seized whatever they pleased. Even the wives and princesses of the great ministers—none dared stand against them.

sentences.zh: 或告居士謀為不軌，帝怒，斬之，公卿子弟坐居士除名者甚眾。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Jushi plotted rebellion. The emperor was enraged and beheaded him; many sons of high ministers who associated with Jushi were struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that Jushi was plotting treason, the emperor had him executed. Many sons of high officials who had kept company with Jushi were struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 楊素、牛弘等復薦張冑玄歷術。

translations.literal: Yang Su, Niu Hong, and others again recommended Zhang Zhouxuan's calendrical arts.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su, Niu Hong, and others again recommended Zhang Zhouxuan for his expertise in calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 上令楊素與術數人立議六十一事，皆舊法久難通者，令劉暉等與冑玄等辯析之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yang Su and men skilled in numerology to set forth sixty-one disputed points—all old methods long difficult to apply—and had Liu Hui and others debate them with Zhouxuan and his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Yang Su and experts in numerology compile sixty-one disputed points—all longstanding flaws in the old calendar—and ordered Liu Hui and others to debate them with Zhouxuan's party.

sentences.zh: 暉杜口一無所答，冑玄通者五十四，上乃拜冑玄員外散騎侍郎兼太史令，賜物千段，令參定新術。

translations.literal: Hui closed his mouth and answered nothing at all; Zhouxuan succeeded on fifty-four points. The emperor then appointed Zhouxuan Extraordinary Cadet of the Chariots and Cavalry and concurrent Director of the Bureau of Astronomy, granted him a thousand lengths of goods, and ordered him to assist in fixing the new calendrical methods.
translations.idiomatic: Hui kept silent and answered not one point. Zhouxuan carried fifty-four. The emperor then made Zhouxuan Extraordinary Cadet of the Chariots and Cavalry and concurrent Director of the Bureau of Astronomy, rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods, and charged him with drafting the new calendar.

sentences.zh: 至是，冑玄歷成。

translations.literal: By this time Zhouxuan's calendar was complete.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhouxuan's calendar was complete.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊寅，詔頒新歷；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wuyin, an edict promulgated the new calendar;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wuyin, an edict promulgated the new calendar.

sentences.zh: 前造歷者劉暉等四人並除名。

translations.literal: The four men who had formerly made the calendar, Liu Hui and the rest, were all struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui and the three other former calendar-makers were all struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，桂州人李世賢反，上議討之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Li Shixian of Guizhou rebelled; the court deliberated suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Li Shixian of Guizhou rebelled, and the court debated sending troops against him.

sentences.zh: 諸將數人請行，上不許，顧右武候大將軍虞慶則曰：「位居宰相，爵乃上公，國家有賊，遂無行意，何也？」

translations.literal: Several generals asked to go; the emperor did not permit it. He turned to Grand General of the Right Martial Guard Yu Qingze and said: "You hold the rank of chancellor and your title is that of grand duke—when the state has bandits, you have no wish to campaign. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Several generals volunteered to lead the campaign, but the emperor refused. He turned to Grand General Yu Qingze of the Right Martial Guard and said, "You hold a chancellor's rank and a grand duke's title—yet when rebels arise you show no zeal to march. Why?"

sentences.zh: 慶則拜謝，恐懼，乃以慶則為桂州道行軍總管，討平之。

translations.literal: Qingze bowed in apology, fearful, and the emperor thereupon made Qingze Commander-in-Chief on the Guizhou Route to suppress and pacify the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Qingze bowed in apology, terrified. The emperor then appointed him Commander-in-Chief on the Guizhou Route, and he put down the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 秦王俊，幼仁恕，喜佛教，嘗請為沙門，不許。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Jun was by nature humane and forgiving in youth, loved Buddhism, and once asked to become a monk—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Jun had been gentle and forgiving since boyhood and loved Buddhism. Once he asked to become a monk, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 及為并州總管，漸好奢侈，違越制度，盛治宮室。

translations.literal: Once he became Commander-in-Chief of Bingzhou he gradually came to love luxury, violated regulations, and lavishly built palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Once made Commander-in-Chief of Bingzhou, he grew fond of luxury, ignored regulations, and spent lavishly on palaces.

sentences.zh: 俊好內，其妃崔氏，弘度之妹也，性妒，於瓜中進毒，由是得疾，征還京師。

translations.literal: Jun loved women. His consort, the Cui lady, was the sister of Hongdu; jealous by nature, she introduced poison in a melon, and he fell ill and was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was fond of women. His consort Lady Cui, sister of Hongdu, was jealous and slipped poison into a melon. He fell ill and was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上以為奢縱，丁亥，免俊官，以王就第。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded this as profligacy and license. On dinghai he removed Jun from office and sent him home as a prince only.
translations.idiomatic: Judging him profligate and ungoverned, on dinghai the emperor stripped Jun of his posts and confined him to his princely residence.

sentences.zh: 崔妃以毒王，廢絕，賜死於家。

translations.literal: Consort Cui for poisoning the prince was deposed and ordered to die at home.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Cui was deposed for poisoning the prince and ordered to die at home.

sentences.zh: 左武衛將軍劉升諫曰：「秦王非有它過，但費官物，營廨捨而已，臣謂可容。」

translations.literal: General of the Left Martial Guard Liu Sheng remonstrated: "The Prince of Qin has no other fault—only that he spent official goods building offices and lodgings. Your servant believes this can be tolerated."
translations.idiomatic: General Liu Sheng of the Left Martial Guard remonstrated, "The Prince of Qin has no other fault than spending official funds on buildings. I believe this can be forgiven."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「法不可違。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The law cannot be violated."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The law cannot be broken."

sentences.zh: 楊素諫曰：「秦王之過，不應至此，願陛下詳之！」

translations.literal: Yang Su remonstrated: "The Prince of Qin's offense does not warrant this—may Your Majesty consider carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su remonstrated, "The prince's offense does not deserve such punishment—I beg Your Majesty to reconsider!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「我是五兒之父，非兆民炎父？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I am the father of five sons—am I not also father and mother to the myriad people?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I am father to five sons—am I not also father and mother to all the people?

sentences.zh: 若如公意，何不別制天子兒律！

translations.literal: If it were as you advise, why not separately devise a law for the Son of Heaven's sons!
translations.idiomatic: If I followed your advice, why not write a separate law for the emperor's sons!

sentences.zh: 以周公之為人，尚誅管、蔡，我誠不及周公遠矣，安能虧法乎！」

translations.literal: Even the Duke of Zhou in his conduct still executed Guan and Cai—how far I truly fall short of the Duke of Zhou! How could I compromise the law!"
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou himself executed Guan and Cai. I am far beneath the Duke of Zhou—how could I bend the law!"

sentences.zh: 卒不許。

translations.literal: In the end he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，突厥突利可汗來逆女，上捨之太常，教習六禮，妻以宗女安義公主。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Tuli Khan of the Turks came to meet his bride. The emperor lodged him at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, taught him the Six Rites, and gave him in marriage the clanswoman, Princess Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Tuli Khan of the Turks arrived to meet his bride. The emperor housed him at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, instructed him in the Six Rites, and married him to the clanswoman Princess Anyi.

sentences.zh: 上欲離間都藍，故特厚其禮，遣太常卿牛弘、納言蘇威、民部尚書斛律孝卿相繼為使。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to sow discord with Dulou; therefore he especially honored Tuli with rich ceremony and sent Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Niu Hong, Chief Minister Su Wei, and Minister of the Household Hulu Xiaqing in succession as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to drive a wedge between Dulou and Tuli, the emperor treated Tuli with exceptional honor and sent Niu Hong, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Chief Minister Su Wei, and Minister of the Household Hulu Xiaqing as envoys in succession.

sentences.zh: 突利本居北方，既尚主，長孫晟說其帥眾南徙，居度斤舊鎮，錫賚優厚。

translations.literal: Tuli had originally dwelt in the north. Once he had married the princess, Zhangsun Sheng persuaded him to lead his people south to resettle at the old fort of Dujin, and he was granted gifts lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli had originally lived in the north. After marrying the princess, Zhangsun Sheng persuaded him to move his people south to the old fort at Dujin, and the court rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 都藍怒曰：「我，大可汗也，反不如染干！」

translations.literal: Dulou said angrily: "I am the great khan—yet I am inferior to Ran'gan!"
translations.idiomatic: Dulou raged, "I am the great khan—yet I rank below Ran'gan!"

sentences.zh: 於是朝貢遂絕，亟來抄掠邊鄙。

translations.literal: Thereupon tribute ceased, and raids on the borderlands came repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute ceased, and he repeatedly raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 突利伺知動靜，輒遣奏聞，由是邊鄙每先有備。

translations.literal: Tuli watched and learned Dulou's movements and always sent reports; therefore the borderlands were each time forewarned and prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli kept watch on Dulou's movements and reported them promptly, so the frontier was always prepared.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲申，上至自仁壽宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiashen, the emperor returned from Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiashen, the emperor returned from Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 何稠之自嶺南還也，寧猛力請隨稠入朝。

translations.literal: When He Chou returned from Lingnan, Ning Mengli asked to follow Chou to court.
translations.idiomatic: When He Chou returned from Lingnan, Ning Mengli asked to accompany him to court.

sentences.zh: 稠見其疾篤，遣還欽州，與之約曰：「八九月間，可詣京師相見。」

translations.literal: Chou saw that he was gravely ill and sent him back to Qinzhou, making an appointment with him: "Between the eighth and ninth months you may come to the capital to meet."
translations.idiomatic: Chou saw that he was deathly ill and sent him back to Qinzhou, promising, "Come to the capital between the eighth and ninth months and we shall meet."

sentences.zh: 使還，奏狀，上意不懌。

translations.literal: After he returned Chou memorialized; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou reported this, the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，猛力病卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Mengli died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Mengli died of illness.

sentences.zh: 上謂稠曰：「汝前不將猛力來，今竟死矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Chou: "You did not bring Mengli before; now he is dead after all!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Chou, "You did not bring Mengli when you could—now he is dead!"

sentences.zh: 稠曰：「猛力與臣約，假令身死，當遣子入侍。

translations.literal: Chou said: "Mengli and I agreed that even should he die, he would send his son to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: Chou said, "Mengli and I agreed that even if he died, he would send his son to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 越人性直，其子必來。」

translations.literal: The Yue people are upright by nature; his son is sure to come."
translations.idiomatic: The Yue are straightforward by nature. His son will surely come."

sentences.zh: 猛力臨終，果戒其子長真曰：「我與大使約，不可失信，汝葬我畢，即宜登路。」

translations.literal: At his end Mengli indeed admonished his son Changzhen: "I made an agreement with the ambassador—it must not be broken. When you have buried me, you should set out at once."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Mengli indeed charged his son Changzhen, "I gave my word to the ambassador. Do not break faith. Once you have buried me, set out at once."

sentences.zh: 長真嗣為刺史，如言入朝。

translations.literal: Changzhen succeeded as prefect and entered court as promised.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhen succeeded as prefect and came to court as promised.

sentences.zh: 上大悅曰：「何稠著信蠻夷，乃至於此！」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "He Chou's good faith among the barbarians reaches even to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted. "He Chou's faith among the barbarians is absolute!"

sentences.zh: 魯公虞慶則之討李世賢也，以婦弟趙什住為隨府長史。

translations.literal: When Duke of Lu Yu Qingze campaigned against Li Shixian, he made his wife's younger brother Zhao Shizhu Chief of Staff of the expedition staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Lu Yu Qingze marched against Li Shixian, he appointed his wife's younger brother Zhao Shizhu chief of staff of the campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 什住通於慶則愛妾，恐事洩，乃宣言慶則不欲此行，上聞之，禮賜甚薄。

translations.literal: Shizhu had an affair with Qingze's favorite concubine. Fearing exposure, he spread word that Qingze did not wish to undertake the campaign. When the emperor heard this, his gifts and honors were very meager.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhu was carrying on with Qingze's favorite concubine. Fearful of exposure, he spread the rumor that Qingze did not want the campaign. When the emperor heard this, his rewards to Qingze were meager indeed.

sentences.zh: 慶則還，至潭州臨桂嶺，觀眺山川形勢，曰：「此誠險固，加以足糧，若守得其人，攻不可拔。」

translations.literal: When Qingze returned and reached Lin Gui Ridge at Tanzhou, he surveyed the terrain and said: "This place is truly defensible. With ample grain, if held by the right man it cannot be taken by assault."
translations.idiomatic: On his return, at Lin Gui Ridge in Tanzhou, Qingze surveyed the terrain and said, "This is a formidable position. With enough grain and the right defender, it could not be taken by assault."

sentences.zh: 使什住馳詣京師奏事，觀上顏色，什住因告慶則謀反，下有司案驗。

translations.literal: He sent Shizhu posthaste to the capital to report; observing the emperor's expression, Shizhu thereupon accused Qingze of plotting rebellion, and the case was referred to the relevant offices for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shizhu posthaste to the capital to report. Reading the emperor's mood, Shizhu accused Qingze of plotting rebellion, and the matter was handed to the judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬子，慶則坐死，拜什住為柱國。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renzi, Qingze was executed for his crime; Shizhu was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renzi, Qingze was executed. Shizhu was made Grand General.

sentences.zh: 高麗王湯聞陳亡，大懼，治兵積穀，為拒守之策。

translations.literal: King Tang of Goguryeo, hearing that Chen had fallen, was greatly afraid. He drilled troops, stored grain, and prepared a strategy of defense.
translations.idiomatic: King Tang of Goguryeo, hearing that Chen had fallen, was terrified. He drilled troops, stockpiled grain, and prepared to resist invasion.

sentences.zh: 是歲，上賜湯璽書，責以「雖稱籓附，誠節未盡」。

translations.literal: That year the emperor sent Tang an imperial letter bearing the seal, rebuking him that "though you call yourself a vassal, your loyal devotion is not complete."
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor sent Tang an imperial letter rebuking him: "Though you call yourself a vassal, your loyalty is incomplete."

sentences.zh: 且曰：「彼之一方，雖地狹人少，今若黜王，不可虛置，終須更選官屬，就彼安撫。

translations.literal: It further said: "That region, though its land is narrow and its people few—if the king were now deposed it could not be left vacant; officials would ultimately have to be chosen afresh and sent to pacify the people there.
translations.idiomatic: It went on, "That land may be small and its people few, but if I remove you, the throne cannot sit empty. Officials would have to be sent to govern and pacify the realm.

sentences.zh: 王若灑心易行，率由憲章，即是朕之良臣，何勞別遣才彥！

translations.literal: If the king cleanses his heart and changes his conduct, following the statutes and ordinances, then he will be Our good minister—what need to send other talented men!
translations.idiomatic: If you purge your heart and reform your ways, obeying the laws, you remain a worthy minister of mine. Why should I send another to replace you?

sentences.zh: 王謂遼水之廣，何如長江？

translations.literal: Does the king think the breadth of the Liao River compares to the Yangzi?
translations.idiomatic: Do you think the Liao River is as wide as the Yangzi?

sentences.zh: 高麗之人，多少陳國？

translations.literal: Are the people of Goguryeo as numerous as those of Chen?
translations.idiomatic: Are the people of Goguryeo as numerous as Chen's?

sentences.zh: 朕若不存含育，責王前愆，命一將軍，何待多力！

translations.literal: If We did not cherish and nurture, and charged the king for past faults, ordering a single general—what need for great forces!
translations.idiomatic: If I were not merciful, I could punish your past offenses with a single general—what need of a great army?

sentences.zh: 殷勤曉示，許王自新耳。」

translations.literal: This is earnest instruction, granting the king permission to renew himself."
translations.idiomatic: I write only to exhort you and offer you a chance to reform."

sentences.zh: 湯得書，惶恐，將奉表陳謝。

translations.literal: Tang received the letter, was fearful, and was about to submit a memorial of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Tang received the letter in terror and prepared a memorial of apology.

sentences.zh: 會病卒，子元嗣立，上使使拜元為上開府儀同三司，襲爵遼東公。

translations.literal: Just then he died of illness. His son Yuan succeeded him. The emperor sent envoys to appoint Yuan as Senior General with Honored Standing of the First Rank and to let him inherit the title Duke of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: But he died before he could. His son Yuan succeeded him. The emperor sent envoys to appoint Yuan Senior General with Honored Standing of the First Rank and to let him inherit the title Duke of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 元奉表謝恩，因請封王，上許之。

translations.literal: Yuan submitted a memorial thanking for the grace and requesting the title of king; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan submitted a memorial of thanks and asked to be made king. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾大亂，國人殺世伏，立其弟伏允為主，遣使陳廢立之事，並謝專命之罪，且請依俗尚主；

translations.literal: Tuyuhun fell into great disorder. The people killed Shifu and installed his younger brother Fuyun as ruler. They sent envoys stating the deposition and installation, apologizing for acting on their own authority, and also requesting a marriage alliance according to custom;
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun fell into chaos. The people killed Shifu and enthroned his brother Fuyun. Envoys came to report the change of rulers, apologize for acting without permission, and request a princess in marriage according to their custom—

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是朝貢歲至。

translations.literal: From then on tribute came every year.
translations.idiomatic: From then on tribute arrived every year.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，甲辰，上幸仁壽宮。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on jiachen, the emperor visited Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on jiachen, the emperor went to Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 高麗王元帥靺鞨之眾萬餘寇遼西，營州總管衝擊韋走之。

translations.literal: King Yuan of Goguryeo led more than ten thousand Mohe troops to raid Liaoxi. Wei Chong, Commander-in-Chief of Yingzhou, routed them.
translations.idiomatic: King Yuan of Goguryeo led more than ten thousand Mohe warriors in a raid on Liaoxi. Wei Chong, Commander-in-Chief of Yingzhou, drove them off.

sentences.zh: 上聞而大怒，乙巳，以漢王諒、王世積並為行軍元帥，將水陸三十萬伐高麗，以尚書左僕射高熲為漢王長史，周羅□為水軍總管。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was greatly enraged. On yisi he made Prince of Han Liang and Wang Shiji both campaign commanders-in-chief, leading three hundred thousand by land and sea to attack Goguryeo; Minister of the Left Gao Jiong was made chief of staff to the Prince of Han, and Zhou Luohou was made naval commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, on yisi the emperor made Prince of Han Liang and Wang Shiji campaign commanders-in-chief, leading three hundred thousand troops by land and sea against Goguryeo. Gao Jiong, Minister of the Left, became chief of staff to Prince Liang, and Zhou Luohou was made naval commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 延州刺史獨孤陀有婢曰徐阿尼，事貓鬼，能使之殺人，雲每殺人，則死家財物潛移於畜貓鬼家。

translations.literal: Yanzhou Inspector Dugu Tuo had a maid named Xu Ani who served the cat demon and could make it kill people. It was said that whenever someone was killed, the dead family's wealth secretly passed to the household that kept the cat demon.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou Inspector Dugu Tuo had a servant girl named Xu Ani who practiced cat-demon sorcery and could send it to kill people. Whenever a victim died, it was said, his family's possessions mysteriously passed to the sorcerer's household.

sentences.zh: 會獨孤後及楊素妻鄭氏俱有疾，醫皆曰：「貓鬼疾也。」

translations.literal: It happened that Empress Dugu and Yang Su's wife Lady Zheng were both ill; physicians all said: "It is cat-demon sickness."
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dugu and Yang Su's wife Lady Zheng both fell ill, physicians declared it cat-demon sickness."

sentences.zh: 上以陀，後之異母弟，陀妻，楊素異母妹，由是意陀所為。

translations.literal: Because Tuo was the empress's half-brother and Tuo's wife was Yang Su's half-sister, the emperor suspected Tuo's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo was the empress's half-brother, and his wife was Yang Su's half-sister. The emperor suspected Tuo was responsible.

sentences.zh: 令高熲等雜治之，具得其實。

translations.literal: He ordered Gao Jiong and others jointly to investigate, and the facts were fully obtained.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Gao Jiong and others to investigate jointly and establish the full truth.

sentences.zh: 上怒，令以犢車載陀夫妻，將賜死。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and ordered Tuo and his wife loaded into an ox cart for execution by imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor ordered Tuo and his wife loaded into an ox cart to be executed.

sentences.zh: 獨孤後三日不食，為之請命曰：「陀若蠹政害民者，妾不敢言；

translations.literal: Empress Dugu fasted for three days and pleaded for his life: "If Tuo has ruined governance and harmed the people, your handmaid dares not speak;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu fasted three days and pleaded for his life. "If Tuo had abused power and harmed the people, I would not speak—

sentences.zh: 今坐為妾身，敢請其命。」

translations.literal: Now that he is punished because of your handmaid's person, I dare request his life."
translations.idiomatic: but he is punished only on my account. I beg you to spare him."

sentences.zh: 陀弟司勳侍郎整詣闕求哀，於是免陀死，除名為民，以其妻楊氏為尼。

translations.literal: Tuo's younger brother, Director of the Directorate of Merits Zheng, came to the palace gate to beg mercy; thereupon Tuo's death was remitted, he was struck from the rolls and made a commoner, and his wife Lady Yang was made a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's brother Zheng, Director of the Directorate of Merits, came to the palace to beg mercy. Tuo was spared death, struck from the rolls, and reduced to commoner status. His wife Lady Yang was made a nun.

sentences.zh: 先是，有人訟其母為貓鬼所殺者，上以為妖妄，怒而遣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, someone had sued claiming his mother was killed by the cat demon; the emperor regarded this as occult delusion, grew angry, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier someone had petitioned that his mother was killed by a cat demon. The emperor dismissed it as occult nonsense and angrily sent him away.

sentences.zh: 至是，詔誅被訟行貓鬼家。

translations.literal: By this time an edict ordered execution of the households accused of practicing the cat demon.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict ordered the execution of every household accused of cat-demon sorcery.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛亥，詔：「畜貓鬼、蠱毒、厭媚野道之家，並投於四裔。」

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinhai, an edict: "Households that keep cat demons, poison by sorcery, or effigy-cursing and wild heresies—all are to be cast to the four peripheries."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinhai, an edict declared: "Households practicing cat-demon sorcery, witch-poisoning, or effigy-cursing are to be exiled to the frontier."

sentences.zh: 六月，丙寅，下詔黜高麗王元官爵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingyin, an edict was issued deposing King Yuan of Goguryeo from office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingyin, an edict stripped King Yuan of Goguryeo of his titles.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒軍出臨渝關，值水潦，饋運不繼，軍中乏食，復遇疾疫。

translations.literal: Prince of Han Liang's army passed out through Linyu Pass, encountered flooding, supply transport could not keep up, the army lacked food, and they also met epidemic sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang's army marched out through Linyu Pass into floods. Supply lines broke down, food ran short, and plague swept the camp.

sentences.zh: 周羅□自東萊泛海趣平壤城，亦遭風，船多飄沒。

translations.literal: Zhou Luohou sailed from Donglai across the sea toward Pyongyang but also met wind; many ships were lost at sea.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Luohou sailed from Donglai toward Pyongyang but ran into storms. Many ships were lost.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，己丑，師還，死者什八九。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on jichou, the army returned; of the dead, eight or nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on jichou, the army withdrew. Eight or nine men in ten had died.

sentences.zh: 高麗王元亦惶懼遣使謝罪，上表稱「遼東糞土臣元」，上於是罷兵，待之如初。

translations.literal: King Yuan of Goguryeo also, in fear, sent envoys to apologize for crimes; he submitted a memorial calling himself "Yuan, subject of the dung and soil of Liaodong"; the emperor thereupon ceased the army and treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: King Yuan of Goguryeo, terrified, sent envoys to apologize. In a memorial he styled himself "Yuan, subject of the worthless soil of Liaodong." The emperor thereupon halted the campaign and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 百濟王昌遣使奉表，請為軍導，帝下詔諭以「高麗服罪，朕已赦之，不可致伐。」

translations.literal: King Chang of Baekje sent envoys with a memorial, requesting to serve as military guide; the emperor issued an edict instructing him: "Goguryeo has submitted and been pardoned; an attack must not be launched."
translations.idiomatic: King Chang of Baekje sent envoys with a memorial offering to guide the army. The emperor replied by edict, "Goguryeo has submitted, and I have already pardoned them. You must not attack them."

sentences.zh: 厚其使而遣之。

translations.literal: He rewarded the envoys generously and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He treated the envoys generously and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 高麗頗知其事，以兵侵掠其境。

translations.literal: Goguryeo learned much of this matter and sent troops to raid and plunder Baekje's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo soon learned of the offer and sent troops to raid Baekje's borders.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上至自仁壽宮。

translations.literal: On xinmao the emperor arrived back from Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the emperor returned from Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，癸未，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on guiwei, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on guiwei, the emperor offered sacrifice at the southern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 十二月，自京師至仁壽宮，置行宮十有二所。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, from the capital to Renshou Palace, twelve traveling palaces were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, twelve traveling palaces were built along the route from the capital to Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 南寧夷爨玩復反。

translations.literal: Cuan Wan of the Nanning Yi rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Cuan Wan of the Nanning Yi rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀奏「史萬歲受賂縱賊，致生邊患。」

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Xiu memorialized: "Shi Wansui accepted bribes and released bandits, causing border troubles."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu Xiu memorialized, "Shi Wansui took bribes and let bandits go free, bringing trouble to the frontier."

sentences.zh: 上責萬歲，萬歲詆讕；

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Wansui; Wansui slandered and denied;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Wansui, who answered with slander and denial.

sentences.zh: 上怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: the emperor grew angry and ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 高熲及左衛大將軍元旻等固請曰：「萬歲雄略過人，將士樂為致力，雖古名將，未能過也。」

translations.literal: Gao Jiong and General of the Left Guard Yuan Min and others firmly pleaded, saying: "Wansui's bold strategy surpasses other men; officers and soldiers gladly exert themselves for him—even ancient famous generals could not surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong, General of the Left Guard Yuan Min, and others urgently pleaded, "Wansui's strategic brilliance surpasses ordinary men. Officers and soldiers gladly give him their utmost—even the great generals of old could not match him."

sentences.zh: 上意少解，於是除名為民。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind eased somewhat; thereupon Wansui was stripped of rank and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented somewhat and instead stripped Wansui of rank, reducing him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸酉，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guiyou, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guiyou, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲寅，上幸仁壽宮。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiayin, the emperor visited Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiayin, the emperor went to Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 突厥突利可汗因長孫晟奏言都藍可汗作攻具，欲攻大同城。

translations.literal: Tuli Khan of the Turks, through Zhangsun Sheng's memorial, reported that Khan Dulou was making siege engines and intended to attack Datong Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Through Zhangsun Sheng's memorial, Tuli Khan reported that Khan Dulou was building siege engines and planned to attack Datong Fort.

sentences.zh: 詔以漢王諒為元帥，尚書左僕射高熲出朔州道，右僕射楊素出靈州道，上柱國燕榮出幽州道以擊都藍，皆取漢王節度；

translations.literal: An edict made Prince of Han Liang commander-in-chief; Minister of the Left Gao Jiong marched by the Shuozhou route, Minister of the Right Yang Su by the Lingzhou route, and Senior Grand Duke Yan Rong by the Youzhou route to strike Dulou—all under Prince Liang's command;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Prince of Han Liang commander-in-chief. Gao Jiong, Minister of the Left, marched by the Shuozhou route; Yang Su, Minister of the Right, by the Lingzhou route; and Senior Grand Duke Yan Rong by the Youzhou route—all to strike Dulou under Prince Liang's command.

sentences.zh: 然漢王竟不臨戎。

translations.literal: yet Prince Liang in the end did not go to the army in person.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang, however, never went to the front in person.

sentences.zh: 都藍聞之，與達頭可汗結盟，合兵掩襲突利，大戰長城下，突利大敗。

translations.literal: Dulou heard of this, allied with Khan Toutou, combined forces in a surprise attack on Tuli, and fought a great battle below the Great Wall; Tuli was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Dulou heard of the campaign, he allied with Khan Toutou and launched a surprise attack on Tuli. They fought a great battle below the Great Wall, and Tuli was routed.

sentences.zh: 都藍盡殺其兄弟子侄，遂渡河入蔚州。

translations.literal: Dulou killed all his brothers, sons, and nephews, then crossed the river and entered Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dulou slaughtered Tuli's brothers, sons, and nephews, then crossed the river and entered Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 突利部落散亡，夜，與長孫晟以五騎南走，比旦，行百餘里，收得數百騎。

translations.literal: Tuli's tribes scattered and fled; at night he and Zhangsun Sheng fled south with five horsemen; by dawn they had gone more than a hundred li and gathered several hundred riders.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli's tribes scattered. That night he fled south with Zhangsun Sheng and five horsemen. By dawn they had ridden more than a hundred li and gathered several hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 突利與其下謀曰：「今兵敗入朝，一降人耳，大隋天子豈禮我乎！

translations.literal: Tuli plotted with his followers, saying: "Now, defeated and entering court, I am only a surrendered man—would the Son of Heaven of Great Sui treat me with ceremony!
translations.idiomatic: Tuli consulted his followers and said, "Defeated and fleeing to court, I am nothing but a surrendered man. Would the Son of Heaven of Great Sui treat me with honor?

sentences.zh: 玷厥雖來，本無冤隙，若往投之，必相存濟。」

translations.literal: Although Dianjue has come, we originally had no feud; if we go and submit to him, he will surely preserve and aid us."
translations.idiomatic: Dianjue is nearby, and we have no old quarrel with him. If we go over to him, he is sure to shelter us."

sentences.zh: 晟知之，密遣使者入伏遠鎮，令速舉烽。

translations.literal: Sheng learned of this and secretly sent a messenger into Fuyuan Garrison, ordering beacons raised at once.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng learned of the plan and secretly sent a messenger to Fuyuan Garrison with orders to raise the beacon fires at once.

sentences.zh: 突利見四烽俱發，以問晟，晟紿之曰：「城高地迥，必遙見賊來。

translations.literal: Tuli saw four beacons all lit and questioned Sheng; Sheng deceived him, saying: "The city is high and the land open; they must have seen the enemy coming from afar.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuli saw all four beacon fires lit, he questioned Sheng. Sheng deceived him, saying, "The garrison sits high on open ground. They must have seen the enemy coming from far off.

sentences.zh: 我國家法，若賊少，舉二烽；

translations.literal: By our state's law, if the enemy are few, two beacons are raised;
translations.idiomatic: By our state's law, if the enemy are few, two beacons are raised;

sentences.zh: 來多，舉三烽；

translations.literal: if many come, three beacons;
translations.idiomatic: if many come, three;

sentences.zh: 大逼，舉四烽。

translations.literal: if they press hard, four beacons.
translations.idiomatic: if they press hard, four.

sentences.zh: 彼見賊多而又近耳。」

translations.literal: They saw many enemies and close at hand, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: They saw a large enemy force close at hand, that is all."

sentences.zh: 突利大懼，謂其眾曰：「追兵己逼，且可投城。」

translations.literal: Tuli was greatly afraid and said to his followers: "Pursuers are already pressing close—we had better take refuge in the city."
translations.idiomatic: Tuli was terrified and told his followers, "Pursuers are already upon us. We had better take refuge in the garrison."

sentences.zh: 既入鎮，晟留其達官執室領其眾，自將突利馳驛入朝。

translations.literal: Once they entered the garrison, Sheng left the high Turkic official Zhishi to lead the followers and himself escorted Tuli by post horse into court.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the garrison, Sheng left Zhishi, a high Turkic official, to lead the followers while he himself escorted Tuli by post horse to the capital.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁酉，突利至長安。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingyou, Tuli reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingyou, Tuli arrived at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，以晟為左勳衛驃騎將軍，持節護突厥。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and made Sheng General of Rapid Cavalry of the Left Merit Guard, bearing the staff to oversee the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and appointed Sheng General of Rapid Cavalry of the Left Merit Guard, with credentials to oversee the Turks.

sentences.zh: 上令突利與都藍使者因頭特勒相辯詰，突利辭直，上乃厚待之。

translations.literal: The emperor had Tuli and Dulou's envoy Yintou teqin debate and cross-examine each other; Tuli's words were straightforward, and the emperor then treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Tuli debate face to face with Dulou's envoy Yintou teqin. Tuli spoke plainly and convincingly, and the emperor treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 都藍弟都速六棄其妻子，與突利歸朝，上嘉之，使突利多遺之珍寶以慰其心。

translations.literal: Dulou's younger brother Dusuliui abandoned his wife and children and came to court with Tuli; the emperor praised this and had Tuli give him many precious gifts to comfort his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Dulou's younger brother Dusuliui abandoned his wife and children and came to court with Tuli. The emperor praised his loyalty and had Tuli give him many precious gifts to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 高熲使上柱國趙仲卿將兵三千為前鋒，至族蠡山，與突厥遇，交戰七日，大破之；

translations.literal: Gao Jiong sent Senior Grand Duke Zhao Zhongqing with three thousand troops as vanguard; reaching Zuli Mountain, they met the Turks, fought for seven days, and routed them;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong sent Senior Grand Duke Zhao Zhongqing ahead with three thousand troops. At Zuli Mountain they met the Turks and fought for seven days before routing them.

sentences.zh: 追奔至乞伏泊，復破之，虜千餘口，雜畜萬計。

translations.literal: pursuing the rout to Qifu Marsh, they defeated them again, capturing more than a thousand persons and livestock numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the fleeing enemy to Qifu Marsh, they defeated them again, capturing more than a thousand people and tens of thousands of livestock.

sentences.zh: 突厥復大舉而至，仲卿為方陳，四面拒戰，凡五日。

translations.literal: The Turks again came in full force; Zhongqing formed a square array and fought on all four sides for five days in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks returned in force. Zhongqing formed a square battle line and fought on all four sides for five days.

sentences.zh: 會高熲大兵至，合擊之，突厥敗走，追度白道，逾秦山七百餘里而還。

translations.literal: When Gao Jiong's main army arrived, they joined in the attack; the Turks were defeated and fled; the pursuit crossed the White Road and went more than seven hundred li beyond Qin Mountain before returning.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jiong's main army arrived, they joined the attack and drove the Turks off. The pursuit crossed the White Road and continued more than seven hundred li beyond Qin Mountain before turning back.

sentences.zh: 楊素軍與達頭遇。

translations.literal: Yang Su's army met Toutou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su's army encountered Toutou.

sentences.zh: 先是諸將與突厥戰，慮其騎兵奔突，皆以戎車步騎相參，設鹿角為方陳，騎在其內。

translations.literal: Earlier, when generals fought the Turks, fearing their cavalry charges, they all mixed war wagons with infantry and cavalry, set antlers as a square formation, and kept the cavalry inside.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when generals fought the Turks, they feared cavalry charges and always mixed war wagons with infantry and cavalry, setting up antler barriers in a square formation with the horsemen inside.

sentences.zh: 素曰：「此乃自固之道，未足以取勝也。」

translations.literal: Su said: "This is only a way to secure oneself—it is not enough to win victory."
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "That is only a way to protect yourself. It is not enough to win."

sentences.zh: 於是悉除舊法，令諸軍為騎陳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he completely abolished the old method and ordered all armies to form cavalry arrays.
translations.idiomatic: He then discarded the old method entirely and ordered his armies to deploy as cavalry formations.

sentences.zh: 達頭聞之，大喜曰：「天賜我也！」

translations.literal: Toutou heard of this and rejoiced greatly, saying: "Heaven has given him to me!"
translations.idiomatic: When Toutou heard of this, he rejoiced and cried, "Heaven has delivered them to me!"

sentences.zh: 下馬仰天而拜，帥騎兵十餘萬直前。

translations.literal: He dismounted, bowed toward Heaven, and led more than a hundred thousand cavalry straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted, bowed toward Heaven, and led more than a hundred thousand horsemen straight at the enemy.

sentences.zh: 上儀同三司周羅□曰：「賊陳未整，請擊之。」

translations.literal: Senior Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhou Luohou said: "The enemy formation is not yet set—please let us attack."
translations.idiomatic: Senior Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhou Luohou said, "The enemy line is not yet formed. Let us attack at once."

sentences.zh: 先帥精騎逆戰，素以大兵繼之，突厥大敗，達頭被重創而遁，殺傷不可勝計，其眾號哭而去。

translations.literal: He first led elite cavalry to meet them in battle; Su followed with the main army; the Turks were utterly defeated; Toutou was gravely wounded and fled; the killed and wounded were beyond counting; his followers wailed as they departed.
translations.idiomatic: He led elite cavalry to meet the charge, and Su followed with the main force. The Turks were routed. Toutou was gravely wounded and fled. The dead and wounded were beyond counting, and his followers wailed as they fled.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁酉，以豫章王暕為內史令。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingyou, Prince of Yuzhang Yang was made Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingyou, Prince of Yuzhang Yang was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宜陽公王世積為涼州總管，其親信安定皇甫孝諧有罪，吏捕之，亡抵世積，世積不納。

translations.literal: Duke of Yiyang Wang Shiji was Area Commander of Liangzhou; his trusted follower Huangfu Xiaoxie of Anding had committed a crime; officials arrested him; he fled and reached Shiji, but Shiji would not shelter him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Yiyang Wang Shiji was Area Commander of Liangzhou. His confidant Huangfu Xiaoxie of Anding was wanted for a crime. When officials came to arrest him, he fled to Shiji, but Shiji refused to shelter him.

sentences.zh: 孝諧配防桂州，因上變，稱「世積嘗令道人相其貴不，道人答曰：『公當為國主，又將之涼州。』

translations.literal: Xiaoxie was assigned to garrison duty at Guizhou; he thereupon submitted a denunciation, saying: "Shiji once had a Daoist read his noble fortune or not; the Daoist answered: 'You are destined to become ruler of the state, and you will also be sent to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxie was sent to garrison duty in Guizhou and submitted a denunciation claiming, "Shiji once had a Daoist read his fortunes. The Daoist answered, 'You are destined to become ruler of the realm, and you will also be sent to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其所親謂世積曰：『河西天下精兵處，可圖大事。』

translations.literal: His close associates said to Shiji: 'Hexi is where the realm's elite troops are gathered—you could plot a great undertaking.'
translations.idiomatic: His intimates then told Shiji, 'Hexi is where the empire's finest troops are gathered. You could plot something great there.'

sentences.zh: 世積曰：『涼州土曠人希，非用武之國。』」

translations.literal: Shiji said: 'Liangzhou's land is broad and its people sparse—it is not a state for wielding arms.'
translations.idiomatic: Shiji replied, 'Liangzhou is vast and sparsely populated. It is no place to raise an army.'

sentences.zh: 世積坐誅，拜孝諧上大將軍。

translations.literal: Shiji was condemned and executed; Xiaoxie was appointed Grand General.'
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was executed for the crime, and Xiaoxie was appointed Grand General.'

sentences.zh: 獨孤后性妨忌，後宮莫敢進御。

translations.literal: Empress Dugu was by nature jealous; in the rear palace none dared approach the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu was fiercely jealous, and no woman in the inner palace dared share the emperor's bed.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥女孫，有美色，先沒宮中。

translations.literal: A granddaughter of Yuwen Kai, of beautiful appearance, had earlier been taken into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: A granddaughter of Yuwen Kai, a woman of striking beauty, had earlier been taken into the palace.

sentences.zh: 上於仁壽宮見而悅之，因得幸。

translations.literal: The emperor saw her at Renshou Palace, was pleased with her, and thus gained her favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw her at Renshou Palace, was taken with her, and slept with her.

sentences.zh: 后伺上聽朝，陰殺之。

translations.literal: The empress waited until the emperor was attending court and secretly had her killed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress waited until the emperor was at court and secretly had the woman killed.

sentences.zh: 上由是大怒，單騎從苑中出，不由徑路，入山谷間二十餘里。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon grew greatly angry, rode out alone from the park, avoided the main path, and entered valleys and hills for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, rode out of the park alone, left the main paths, and plunged more than twenty li into the hills.

sentences.zh: 高熲、楊素等追及上，扣馬苦諫。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong, Yang Su, and others caught up with the emperor, grasped his horse's bridle, and urgently remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong, Yang Su, and others caught up with him, seized his bridle, and pleaded with him urgently.

sentences.zh: 上太息曰：「吾貴為天子，不得自由！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed deeply and said: "I am exalted as Son of Heaven, yet I cannot be free!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "I am Son of Heaven, yet I am not even free!"

sentences.zh: 高熲曰：「陛下豈以一婦人而輕天下！」

translations.literal: Gao Jiong said: "Your Majesty, would you for one woman slight all under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong said, "Your Majesty, would you throw away the empire for one woman!"

sentences.zh: 上意少解，駐馬良久，中夜方還宮。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind eased somewhat; he halted his horse for a long time and only at midnight returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented somewhat. He reined in his horse and remained there a long time, returning to the palace only at midnight.

sentences.zh: 后俟上於閣內，及至，后流涕拜謝，熲、素等和解之，因置酒極歡。

translations.literal: The empress waited for the emperor inside the pavilion; when he arrived, the empress wept and bowed in apology; Jiong, Su, and others reconciled them, and they then set out wine and rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The empress waited for him inside the pavilion. When he arrived, she wept and bowed in apology. Jiong, Su, and the others helped reconcile them, and a feast was held in great good humor.

sentences.zh: 先是后以高熲父之家客，甚見親禮，至是，聞熲謂己為一婦人，遂銜之。

translations.literal: Earlier the empress, as a guest in Gao Jiong's father's household, had been treated with great intimacy and courtesy; now, hearing Jiong call her "one woman," she therefore harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had once been a guest in Gao Jiong's father's household and had been treated with great kindness. Now, hearing Jiong call her "one woman," she nursed a grievance against him.

sentences.zh: 時太子勇失愛於上，潛有廢立之志，從容謂熲曰：「有神告晉王妃，言王必有天下，若之何？」

translations.literal: At that time Crown Prince Yong had lost the emperor's favor and secretly harbored thoughts of deposition and installation; at leisure he said to Jiong: "A spirit told the consort of the Prince of Jin that the prince would surely gain all under Heaven—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong had fallen from favor and secretly contemplated removing himself from succession. At leisure he said to Jiong, "A spirit told the consort of Prince of Jin Guang that the prince would surely gain the throne. What should be done?"

sentences.zh: 熲長跪曰：「長幼有序，其可廢乎！」

translations.literal: Jiong knelt long and said: "Elder and younger have their order—how can he be deposed!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiong knelt and said, "Elder and younger have their proper order. How can the heir be set aside!"

sentences.zh: 上默然而止。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 獨孤后知熲不可奪，陰欲去之。

translations.literal: Empress Dugu knew Jiong could not be moved and secretly wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu knew Jiong could not be swayed and secretly resolved to remove him.

sentences.zh: 會上令選東宮衛士以入上台，熲奏稱：「若盡取強者，恐東宮宿衛太劣。」

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor ordered selection of Eastern Palace guards to enter the Upper Platform guard; Jiong memorialized, saying: "If all the strongest are taken, I fear the Eastern Palace night guard will be too weak."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered guards from the Eastern Palace transferred to his own guard, Jiong memorialized, "If all the strongest men are taken, the Eastern Palace guard will be left too weak."

sentences.zh: 上作色曰：「我有時出入，宿衛須得勇毅。

translations.literal: The emperor changed countenance and said: "When I go in and out, the night guard must be brave and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened. "When I go abroad, my guard must be brave and resolute.

sentences.zh: 太子毓德東宮，左右何須壯士！

translations.literal: The crown prince cultivates virtue in the Eastern Palace—why do his attendants need strong warriors!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is cultivating virtue in the Eastern Palace. Why does he need strong warriors at his side!

sentences.zh: 此極弊法。

translations.literal: This is an extremely corrupt practice.
translations.idiomatic: That is a thoroughly corrupt practice.

sentences.zh: 如我意者，恆於交番之日，分向東宮，上下團伍不別，豈非佳事！

translations.literal: As I see it, whenever guard rotation comes, they should be divided toward the Eastern Palace without distinction between upper and lower units and squads—would that not be an excellent thing!
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, on every rotation day the guards should be divided between my palace and the Eastern Palace without distinction of rank or unit. Would that not be better!

sentences.zh: 我熟見前代，公不須仍踵舊風。」

translations.literal: I have seen former ages clearly—you, sir, need not still follow the old ways."
translations.idiomatic: I know the precedents of earlier dynasties well. You need not cling to the old ways."

sentences.zh: 熲子表仁，娶太子女，故上以此言防之。

translations.literal: Jiong's son Biaoren had married the crown prince's daughter; therefore the emperor spoke thus to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's son Biaoren had married the crown prince's daughter, so the emperor spoke in this way to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 熲夫人卒，獨孤后言於上曰：「高僕射老矣，而喪夫人，陛下何能不為之娶！」

translations.literal: Jiong's wife died; Empress Dugu said to the emperor: "Vice Director Gao is old, and he has lost his wife—Your Majesty, how can you not find him a new marriage!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong's wife died, Empress Dugu said to the emperor, "Vice Director Gao is growing old and has lost his wife. Your Majesty, surely you should find him a new match!"

sentences.zh: 上以後言告熲。

translations.literal: The emperor told Jiong what the empress had said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeated the empress's words to Jiong.

sentences.zh: 熲流涕謝曰：「臣今已老，退朝，唯齋居讀佛經而已。

translations.literal: Jiong wept and apologized, saying: "Your servant is now old; after court I only dwell in fasting quarters reading Buddhist sutras, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong wept and declined, saying, "I am old now. After court I live quietly, reading Buddhist sutras and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 雖陛下垂哀之深，至於納室，非臣所願。」

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty's compassion runs deep, as for taking a new chamber, it is not what your servant wishes."
translations.idiomatic: However deep Your Majesty's kindness, taking a new wife is not what I wish."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 既而熲愛妾生男，上聞之，極喜，後甚不悅。

translations.literal: Soon after, Jiong's favorite concubine bore a son; when the emperor heard this he was extremely pleased, but the empress was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jiong's favorite concubine bore a son. The emperor was delighted, but the empress was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 上問其故，后曰：「陛下尚覆信高熲邪？

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; the empress said: "Your Majesty, do you still trust Gao Jiong after all?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked why, the empress said, "Your Majesty, do you still trust Gao Jiong?

sentences.zh: 始，陛下欲為熲娶，熲心存愛妾，面欺陛下。

translations.literal: At first, when Your Majesty wished to find Jiong a wife, Jiong kept his favorite concubine in his heart and deceived Your Majesty to his face.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty offered to find him a wife, Jiong already had a favorite concubine and lied to Your Majesty's face.

sentences.zh: 今其詐已見，安得信之！」

translations.literal: Now his deceit has been exposed—how can he be trusted!"
translations.idiomatic: Now his deceit is plain. How can he be trusted!"

sentences.zh: 上由是疏熲。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon grew distant from Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the emperor grew distant from Jiong.

sentences.zh: 伐遼之役，熲固諫，不從，及師無功，后言於上曰：「熲初不欲行，陛下強遣之，妾固知其無功矣！」

translations.literal: In the campaign against Liaodong, Jiong firmly remonstrated but was not heeded; when the army achieved no success, the empress said to the emperor: "Jiong from the first did not wish to go; Your Majesty forced him to go—I knew all along it would come to nothing!"
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign Jiong had strongly remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen. When the army returned without success, the empress said, "Jiong never wanted to go. Your Majesty forced him. I knew all along it would fail!"

sentences.zh: 又，上以漢王年少，專委軍事於熲，熲以任寄隆重，每懷至公，無自疑之意，諒所言多不用。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Prince Liang was young, the emperor entrusted military affairs exclusively to Jiong; Jiong, because the commission was weighty, always held utmost public-mindedness and had no thought of self-doubt; Liang's words were mostly not adopted.
