translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because Prince Liang was young, the emperor entrusted military affairs entirely to Jiong. Jiong, mindful of the weight of that trust, always acted with utmost impartiality and paid no heed to self-interest. Most of Liang's suggestions went unused.

sentences.zh: 諒甚銜之，及還，泣言於后曰：「兒倖免高熲所殺。」

translations.literal: Liang deeply resented this; when he returned, he wept and said to the empress: "Your son barely escaped being killed by Gao Jiong."
translations.idiomatic: Liang deeply resented this. When he returned, he wept and told the empress, "Your son barely escaped death at Gao Jiong's hands."

sentences.zh: 上聞之，彌不平。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he grew all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, his displeasure with Jiong only deepened.

sentences.zh: 及擊突厥，出白道，進圖入磧，遣使請兵，近臣緣此言熲欲反。

translations.literal: When he attacked the Turks, marched out by the White Road, advanced planning to enter the desert, and sent envoys requesting reinforcements, close ministers seized on this to say Jiong intended rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against the Turks, after marching out by the White Road and advancing into the desert, Jiong sent envoys requesting reinforcements. Court favorites seized on this to claim he was plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上未有所答，熲已破突厥而還。

translations.literal: The emperor had not yet replied when Jiong had already defeated the Turks and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor could respond, Jiong had already defeated the Turks and returned.

sentences.zh: 及王世積誅，推核之際，有宮禁中事，云於熲處得之，上大驚。

translations.literal: When Wang Shiji was executed, during the investigation there were matters from within the palace precincts said to have been obtained at Jiong's place; the emperor was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shiji was executed, the investigation turned up palace secrets said to have come from Jiong's household. The emperor was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 有司又奏「熲及左右衛大將軍元旻、元冑，並與世積交通，受其名馬之贈。」

translations.literal: The officials also memorialized: "Jiong and Generals of the Left and Right Guard Yuan Min and Yuan Zhou all had dealings with Shiji and accepted famous horses from him."
translations.idiomatic: The officials also reported, "Jiong, along with Generals of the Left and Right Guard Yuan Min and Yuan Zhou, had dealings with Shiji and accepted prized horses from him."

sentences.zh: 旻、冑坐免官。

translations.literal: Min and Zhou were condemned and removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Min and Zhou were stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 上柱國賀若弼、吳州總管宇文弼、刑部尚書薛冑、民部尚書斛律孝卿、兵部尚書柳述等明熲無罪，上愈怒，皆以屬吏，自是朝臣無敢言者。

translations.literal: Senior Grand Duke He Ruobi, Area Commander of Wuzhou Yuwen Bi, Minister of Justice Xue Zhou, Minister of Revenue Hulü Xiaoqing, Minister of War Liu Shu, and others declared Jiong innocent; the emperor grew angrier still and had them all turned over to the judicial officers; from this time no court minister dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Senior Grand Duke He Ruobi, Area Commander of Wuzhou Yuwen Bi, Minister of Justice Xue Zhou, Minister of Revenue Hulü Xiaoqing, Minister of War Liu Shu, and others declared Jiong innocent. The emperor grew still angrier and had them all handed over to the judicial officers. From then on no court minister dared speak up for Jiong.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，癸卯，熲坐免上柱國、左僕射，以齊公就第。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on guimao, Jiong was condemned and removed from Senior Grand Duke and Minister of the Left; as Duke of Qi he retired to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on guimao, Jiong was stripped of his rank as Senior Grand Duke and Minister of the Left and sent home as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上幸秦王俊第，召熲侍宴。

translations.literal: Before long, the emperor visited Prince of Qin Jun's residence and summoned Jiong to attend the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor visited Prince of Qin Jun's residence and summoned Jiong to join the banquet.

sentences.zh: 熲歔欷悲不自勝，獨孤后亦對之泣。

translations.literal: Jiong sobbed and grieved beyond control; Empress Dugu also wept facing him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong wept until he could no longer contain himself, and Empress Dugu wept as she looked on.

sentences.zh: 上謂熲曰：「朕不負公，公自負也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Jiong: "I have not failed you—you have failed yourself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Jiong, "I have not failed you. You have failed yourself."

sentences.zh: 因謂侍臣曰：「我於高熲，勝於兒子，雖或不見，常似目前。

translations.literal: He then told the attending ministers: "Toward Gao Jiong I am closer than to a son; though I may not see him, he is always as if before my eyes.
translations.idiomatic: He then told his attendants, "My bond with Gao Jiong is closer than with a son. Even when I do not see him, he is always before my eyes.

sentences.zh: 自其解落，瞑然忘之，如本無高熲。

translations.literal: Since his dismissal I have forgotten him in darkness, as if there had never been a Gao Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Since I removed him from office I have forgotten him entirely, as though Gao Jiong had never existed.

sentences.zh: 人臣不可以身要君，自雲第一也。」

translations.literal: A minister may not use his person to coerce his ruler and call himself first."
translations.idiomatic: A subject must not hold his ruler hostage to his own importance and proclaim himself indispensable."

sentences.zh: 頃之，熲國令上熲陰事，稱其子表仁謂熲曰：「司馬仲達初托疾不朝，遂有天下。

translations.literal: Before long Jiong's state chief reported Jiong's secret affairs, saying his son Biaoren told Jiong: "Sima Zhongda at first feigned illness and did not attend court, and thereby gained the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jiong's chief of staff reported his secret dealings, alleging that his son Biaoren had told him, "Sima Zhongda first feigned illness and stayed away from court, and in the end he won the realm.

sentences.zh: 公今遇此，焉知非福！」

translations.literal: Sir, meeting this now—how do you know it is not a blessing!"
translations.idiomatic: You face the same situation now. Who is to say it may not prove a blessing!"

sentences.zh: 於是上大怒，囚熲於內史省而鞫之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor was greatly enraged, imprisoned Jiong in the Secretariat and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, imprisoned Jiong in the Secretariat, and interrogated him.

sentences.zh: 憲司復奏沙門真覺嘗謂熲云：「明年國有大喪。」

translations.literal: The censorate again reported that the monk Zhenjue had once told Jiong: "Next year the state will have a great mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The censorate further reported that the monk Zhenjue had once told Jiong, "Next year the state will suffer a great bereavement."

sentences.zh: 尼令暉復云：「十七、十八年，皇帝有大厄，十九年不可過。」

translations.literal: The nun Linghui also said: "In the seventeenth and eighteenth years the emperor will have a great calamity; the nineteenth year he cannot pass."
translations.idiomatic: The nun Linghui had also said, "In the seventeenth and eighteenth years the emperor will face grave peril, and he will not survive the nineteenth."

sentences.zh: 上聞而益怒，顧謂群臣曰：「帝王豈可力求！

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he grew still angrier and, turning to the ministers, said: "Can an emperor's throne be seized by force!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this he grew still angrier and said to his ministers, "Can an emperor's throne be seized by force!

sentences.zh: 孔子以大聖之才，猶不得天下。

translations.literal: Confucius, with the talent of the greatest sage, still could not gain the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, for all his supreme wisdom, never won the realm.

sentences.zh: 熲與子言，自比晉帝，此何心乎！」

translations.literal: Jiong spoke with his son and compared himself to the Jin emperor—what sort of heart is this!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiong spoke with his son and compared himself to an emperor of Jin. What was he thinking!"

sentences.zh: 有司請斬之。

translations.literal: The responsible offices requested his execution.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices asked that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「去年殺虞慶則，今茲斬王世積，如更誅熲，天下其謂我何！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Last year I killed Yu Qingze; this year I executed Wang Shiji—if I also put Jiong to death, what will the realm say of me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Last year I killed Yu Qingze, and this year I executed Wang Shiji. If I also execute Jiong, what will the realm say of me!"

sentences.zh: 於是除名為民。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was struck from the rolls and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore struck from the rolls and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 熲初為僕射，其母戒之曰：「汝富貴已極，但有一斫頭耳，爾其慎之！」

translations.literal: When Jiong first became Vice Director, his mother warned him: "Your wealth and honor have reached the limit—there is only one beheading left; be careful!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong first became Vice Director, his mother warned him, "You have reached the summit of wealth and honor. Only one thing remains—a beheading. Take care!"

sentences.zh: 熲由是常恐禍變。

translations.literal: From this Jiong always feared disaster.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Jiong lived in constant fear of calamity.

sentences.zh: 至是，熲歡然無恨色。

translations.literal: At this time Jiong was cheerful with no look of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When his fall came, Jiong accepted it cheerfully, without a trace of bitterness.

sentences.zh: 先是國子祭酒元善言於上曰：「楊素粗疏，蘇威怯懦，元冑、元熲正似鴨耳。

translations.literal: Earlier the National University Chancellor Yuan Shan had told the emperor: "Yang Su is coarse and careless, Su Wei timid and weak; Yuan Zhou and Yuan Jiong are just like ducks.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier National University Chancellor Yuan Shan had told the emperor, "Yang Su is crude and careless, Su Wei timid and weak. Yuan Zhou and Yuan Jiong are no better than ducks.

sentences.zh: 可以付社稷者，唯獨高熲。」

translations.literal: The one who can be entrusted with the altars of state is Gao Jiong alone."
translations.idiomatic: Only Gao Jiong can be entrusted with the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 上初然之。

translations.literal: At first the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 及熲得罪，上深責之，善憂懼而卒。

translations.literal: When Jiong was punished, the emperor deeply blamed Shan; Shan, anxious and fearful, died.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong fell, the emperor blamed Shan harshly. Shan died soon afterward, consumed by fear and grief.

sentences.zh: 九月，以太常卿牛弘為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Niu Hong was made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Niu Hong was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 弘選舉先德行而後文才，務在審慎，雖致停緩，其所進用，並多稱職。

translations.literal: Hong in selection put moral conduct first and literary talent after, striving for carefulness; though this caused delay, those he advanced were mostly competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: Hong ranked moral conduct above literary talent in appointments. He was deliberately cautious, and though the process moved slowly, most of those he advanced proved competent.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎高孝基鑒賞機晤，清慎絕倫，然爽俊有餘，跡似輕薄，時宰多以此疑之；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Gao Xiaoji was discerning and quick-witted, pure and careful beyond compare, yet he had surplus brilliance and ease, his traces seeming frivolous—contemporary chancellors often doubted him on this account;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Gao Xiaoji was brilliant and exceptionally upright, yet his manner was so quick and sharp that many senior officials suspected him of being frivolous;

sentences.zh: 唯弘深識其真，推心任委。

translations.literal: only Hong deeply knew his true quality and entrusted him with open heart.
translations.idiomatic: only Hong saw his true worth and entrusted him wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 隋之選舉得人，於斯為最，時論彌服弘識度之遠。

translations.literal: Of Sui's selections that gained worthy men, this was the finest; contemporary opinion increasingly admired Hong's far-reaching judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Never did the Sui court choose officials so well as under Hong, and contemporaries admired his foresight all the more.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲午，以突厥突利可汗為意利珍豆啟民可汗，華言意智健也。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiawu, the Türk Khan Tuli was made Khan Qimin of Yilizhendou; in Chinese this means wise and vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiawu, the Türk Khan Tuli was enthroned as Qimin Khan Yilizhendou—a Chinese rendering meaning wise and vigorous.

sentences.zh: 突厥歸啟民者男女萬餘口，上命長孫晟將五萬人於朔州築大利城以處之。

translations.literal: Türks who submitted to Qimin numbered more than ten thousand men and women; the emperor ordered Zhangsun Sheng to lead fifty thousand men to build Dali City at Shuozhou to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand Türks submitted to Qimin. The emperor ordered Zhangsun Sheng to lead fifty thousand men to build Dali City at Shuozhou to settle them.

sentences.zh: 時安義公主已卒，復使晟持節送宗女義成公主以妻之。

translations.literal: At the time the Princess of Righteousness had died; again Sheng was sent bearing credentials to escort the imperial clanswoman Princess Yicheng to be his wife.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Righteousness had by then died, so the emperor again sent Sheng with credentials to escort the clanswoman Princess Yicheng as Qimin's bride.

sentences.zh: 晟奏：「染幹部落，歸者益眾，雖在長城之內，猶被雍虞閭抄掠，不得寧居。

translations.literal: Sheng memorialized: "Ran'gan's tribes—those who submit grow ever more numerous; though within the Long Wall, they are still raided by Yongyu Lubu and cannot live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng memorialized, "Ran'gan's followers grow daily, yet even inside the Long Wall they are still raided by Yongyu Lubu and cannot live in peace.

sentences.zh: 請徙五原，以河為固，於夏、勝兩州之間，東西至河，南北四百里，掘為橫塹，令處其內，使得任情畜牧。」

translations.literal: Request to move them to Wuyuan, using the river as defense; between Xia and Sheng prefectures, east and west to the river, north and south four hundred li, dig a transverse trench, let them dwell within, and allow them to pasture at will."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be moved to Wuyuan, using the Yellow River as a barrier. Between Xia and Sheng prefectures, four hundred li from east to west and from north to south, let a trench be dug and the tribes settled within it so they may pasture freely."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又令上柱國趙仲卿屯兵二萬為啟民防達頭，代州總管韓洪等將步騎一萬鎮恆安。

translations.literal: He also ordered Grand General Zhao Zhongqing to station twenty thousand troops to defend Qimin against Datou; the overall commander of Daizhou Han Hong and others led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Heng'an.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Grand General Zhao Zhongqing to station twenty thousand troops to shield Qimin from Datou, while Han Hong, overall commander of Daizhou, and others led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Heng'an.

sentences.zh: 達頭騎十萬來寇，韓洪軍大敗，仲卿自樂寧鎮邀擊，斬首虜千餘級。

translations.literal: Datou came raiding with one hundred thousand horsemen; Han Hong's army was greatly defeated; Zhongqing from Leling town intercepted and struck, beheading and capturing more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Datou invaded with one hundred thousand horsemen and routed Han Hong's army. Zhongqing intercepted him from Leling and killed or captured more than a thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 帝遣越公楊素出靈州，行軍總管韓僧壽出慶州。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Duke of Yue Yang Su out from Lingzhou and Campaign Commander-in-Chief Han Shoushou out from Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Duke of Yue Yang Su from Lingzhou and Campaign Commander-in-Chief Han Shoushou from Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平公史萬歲出燕州，大將軍武威姚辯出河州，以擊都藍。

translations.literal: Duke of Taiping Shi Wansui went out from Yanzhou; Grand General Weiwu Yao Bian went out from Hezhou—to attack Dulou.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Taiping Shi Wansui marched from Yanzhou, and Grand General Weiwu Yao Bian from Hezhou, all to strike Dulou.

sentences.zh: 師未出塞，十二月，乙未，都藍為部下所殺，達頭自立為步迦可汗，其國大亂。

translations.literal: Before the armies left the frontier, in the twelfth month on yiwei Dulou was killed by his subordinates; Datou made himself Khan Bujia, and the state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Before the armies crossed the frontier, in the twelfth month, on yiwei, Dulou was killed by his own followers. Datou proclaimed himself Khan Bujia, and the Türk realm fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 長孫晟言於上曰：「今官軍臨境，戰數有功，虜內自攜離，其主被殺，乘此招撫，可以盡降。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Sheng said to the emperor: "Now the imperial armies are at the border, fighting repeatedly with merit; within the barbarians they turn against one another, their lord is killed—seize this to summon and soothe, and all can be made to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Sheng told the emperor, "Our armies stand at the border with repeated victories. The barbarians are tearing one another apart and their khan is dead. If we seize this moment to offer terms, we can bring them all to submission.

sentences.zh: 請遣染幹部下分道招慰。」

translations.literal: Request to send Ran'gan's subordinates in separate routes to summon and comfort."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Ran'gan's followers be sent out in separate columns to offer surrender terms."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 降者甚眾。

translations.literal: Those who submitted were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: A great multitude submitted.
